item.title: Fed's Musalem says tighter monetary policy needed to lower inflation
item.description: St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem said on Thursday the US central bank will need to hike interest rates again to bring inflation back to its 2% target, although he declined to say what policymakers should do at their meeting later this month.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem said on Thursday the US central bank will need to hike interest rates again to bring [USN:L1N45M0L0 TEXT:"inflation back"] to its 2% target, although he declined to say what policymakers should do at their meeting later this month. "To bring inflation back to target in a timely manner, more monetary policy firming will be required," Musalem said at an event held by Bloomberg in New York. "If a timely manner is something like 18 months, that kind of suggests that rates ought to be going up further in an appropriate period of time in the next six to nine months," he said. Musalem, who is not a voting member of the central bank's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee this year, demurred when asked if the Fed should raise rates at the October 27-28 meeting. "I go into every meeting with a very open mind, and I haven't prejudged what the outcome of that meeting is going to be, or what I'm going to do at that meeting," Musalem said, adding that the general direction of "inflation requires us to be thinking of further policy firming here." Traders broadly expect the Fed will hold its policy rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range at the meeting in October. The Fed [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"hiked rates"] at its September 15-16 meeting in an effort to bring high levels of inflation back to its target. Policymakers at that meeting also penciled in another rate hike by the end of this year. Traders had been putting strong odds on an October rate hike until New York Fed President John Williams said last week that there is [USN:S0N44V01O TEXT:"no urgency to act"] while the Fed weighs incoming data. Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson followed up by saying he saw no imminent need to raise rates. The Fed is now expected to deliver its next rate hike in December. 'UNSUSTAINABLE FISCAL PATH' In his remarks, Musalem said inflation is the economy's primary problem amid strong growth and a stable job market. He said the Fed can likely lower inflation without denting hiring, and that getting inflation back to the 2% goal would be broadly helpful. Musalem also noted that even with the notable rise in bond yields, "financial conditions remain accommodative and supportive of economic growth." He said the rise in yields does not signal investors are losing confidence in the Fed. Instead, yields are up on expectations that real rates will go up in a strong economy marked by a lot of competition for capital. Strong investment in the tech sector and large government borrowing needs are helping to keep yields up, he said. "The US federal government has been on an unsustainable fiscal path now for the better part of two decades," Musalem said, adding that "the risk is there" that heavy levels of government borrowing could create [USN:L6N45T16X TEXT:"problems"] for the economy.

item.title: Rosa prevê superávit comercial de ao menos US$90 bi em 2026, acima de estimativa oficial
item.description: O Brasil deve ter um superávit comercial de ao menos US$90 bilhões este ano a despeito da recente redução da estimativa oficial do governo para um saldo de cerca de US$85 bilhões, disse nesta quinta-feira o ministro de Indústria Comércio Bens e Serviços, Márcio Elias Rosa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Brasil deve ter um superávit comercial de ao menos US$90 bilhões este ano a despeito da recente redução da estimativa oficial do governo para um saldo de cerca de US$85 bilhões, disse nesta quinta-feira o ministro de Indústria Comércio Bens e Serviços, Márcio Elias Rosa. Segundo ele , o país vem apostando na diversificação de mercados para compensar o impacto sobre as exportações de movimentos como o tarifaço dos EUA e o embargo a carnes bovinas e de aves imposto pela União Europeia. “Continuo apostando em US$90 bilhões, se não passar de US$90 bilhões", disse ele a jornalistas na Firjan (Federação das Indústrias do Estado do Rio de Janeiro). Rosa disse que as negociações para flexibilização do tarifaço norte-americano estão caminhando e em três ou quatro semanas o governo brasileiro espera receber uma nova [USN:L1N45M15C TEXT:"proposta"] dos EUA. "Nós podemos constituir um grupo de trabalho, se for o caso, enquanto isso as equipes técnicas podem dialogar." O Mdic reduziu na terça-feira sua projeção para o superávit da balança comercial brasileira em 2026 a US$84,4 bilhões, contra previsão feita em julho de saldo de US$90 bilhões, prevendo ganho menor nas exportações e arrefecimento de preços internacionais. Apesar da revisão para baixo, o resultado ainda seria 24% mais forte do que o observado no ano anterior, quando o saldo foi de US$68,1 bilhões, e marcaria o segundo maior saldo da série histórica, atrás apenas do dado de 2023.

item.title: Mandados de busca contra ex-príncipe Andrew são anulados após polícia admitir erro jurídico
item.description: A polícia britânica informou na quinta-feira que os mandados de busca obtidos para revistar imóveis ligados a Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor foram emitidos ilegalmente e têm de ser anulados, mas disse que a investigação sobre o irmão mais novo do rei Charles continua em andamento.
item.dc:creator: Michael Holden
item.content:encoded: A polícia britânica informou na quinta-feira que os mandados de busca obtidos para revistar imóveis ligados a Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor foram emitidos ilegalmente e têm de ser anulados, mas disse que a investigação sobre o irmão mais novo do rei Charles continua em andamento. Mountbatten-Windsor, de 66 anos, foi preso em fevereiro sob suspeita de prevaricação no exercício de cargo público, devido à sua relação com o falecido criminoso sexual norte-americano Jeffrey Epstein, e foram realizadas buscas em propriedades em Sandringham, no leste da Inglaterra, e em Windsor. A prisão do membro sênior da realeza, oitavo na linha de sucessão ao trono, foi sem precedentes na era moderna, e uma foto da Reuters do ex-príncipe, com o rosto pálido, saindo da delegacia de polícia, foi manchete em jornais de todo o mundo. No entanto, posteriormente, Mountbatten-Windsor, que não fez nenhum comentário público desde sua prisão, entrou com uma ação judicial e solicitou a anulação dos mandados de busca. A Polícia de Thames Valley afirmou que agora concorda que os mandados não foram devidamente concedidos pelos tribunais. “Aceitamos a posição de que a decisão inicial do tribunal de emitir mandados com base na legislação específica utilizada foi incorreta e, portanto, estes devem ser legalmente anulados”, disse um porta-voz da Polícia de Thames Valley. “Atualmente, estão em andamento procedimentos judiciais para decidir como o material apreendido durante as buscas será tratado e se podemos retê-lo legalmente para apoiar nossa investigação em andamento.” Em uma audiência no Tribunal Superior de Londres na quinta-feira, o juiz Nicholas Hilliard afirmou que a polícia estava solicitando a retenção dos bens apreendidos, o que Mountbatten-Windsor contestava, e que a questão não seria resolvida até o próximo ano. Um porta-voz da Polícia de Thames Valley afirmou que não havia devolvido nenhum material à família real, exceto aquele que não foi considerado relacionado à investigação. A polícia disse que sua investigação, que se refere ao período em que Mountbatten-Windsor atuou como representante especial britânico para o comércio, entre 2001 e 2011, seria demorada e extremamente complexa. Ele foi forçado a renunciar a todas as funções oficiais da realeza em 2019 devido a seus laços com Epstein e, em seguida, foi destituído de seus títulos e honrarias por seu irmão mais velho em outubro passado, após novas revelações sobre o relacionamento entre os dois. Epstein foi encontrado morto em sua cela na prisão de Manhattan em agosto de 2019, em um caso considerado suicídio.

item.title: Law firms give lawyers time off billing grind to test-drive AI
item.description: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com)
item.dc:creator: Sara Merken, David Thomas
item.content:encoded: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com ) As Ropes & Gray ramps up its use of AI, the law firm said its 1,000-plus associates and counsel can now count up to 100 hours of AI experimenting and training toward their annual billing requirements. The move, part of a firmwide AI training initiative in place since the spring, expands on the firm's decision last year to allow first-year associates to [USN:L1N3WF0V8 TEXT:"devote up to 20% of their required billable hours"] – nearly 400 hours – to AI training and simulations. All of Boston-founded Ropes' first-year associates participated in the program, which the firm found to be a "huge success," said Patrick Ryan, its director of knowledge management innovation. A Ropes spokesperson said the firm has "invested over 35,000 associate hours to AI time this year," but did not specify if those hours were all included under the hourly-credit program. Law firms use hourly requirements to ensure lawyers are busy, assess their productivity and allocate bonuses. Devoting a portion of them to non-client work is another sign of the legal industry's investment in AI, which firms are using to speed up legal work and streamline their business operations. Two Ropes associates told Reuters the credit program gives them flexibility to try AI tools even when it can't be billed directly to clients. Kevin Schoonveld, a New York-based ninth-year debt finance associate, said learning to use prompts that yield accurate results takes time that busy associates might otherwise be less willing to commit. “When you're first playing around with these AI tools, you're investing a lot of time in it and you're not seeing a ton of efficiencies at first," he said. Some other firms are also allowing limited billable hours credits for work using AI that’s not directly for clients. At Akerman, lawyers since April have been able to get credit for AI-related projects that are “really contributing value” to the firm, said chairman Scott Meyers. He said the firm posts AI assignments on an internal portal for associates to take up or propose their own. So far, associate projects have included building an AI agent to review construction contracts and testing AI research tools to document where they have produced inaccurate results, he said. “We understand that there may be some compression in billable hours” due to AI being able to handle more work, Meyers said. But he said that alone shouldn't dictate a need for fewer associates, and the credits program helps to address associates' concerns about AI's impact on the time they're billing. “If we need to find other ways to fill that time, I suspect it will be that combination of billable and creditable hours,” he said. As at most large firms, billable hours credits are also allocated for pro bono work. At Ropes & Gray, the AI credits are part of a broader training and professional development program for all the firm's attorneys. Lawyers move through training modules toward applying AI to client work and are later encouraged to develop internal AI tools or processes, Ryan said. The firm is also including AI as a topic in lawyers' annual review conversations, but not with the aim of penalizing them, said Amy Ross, the firm's chief legal talent officer. "To the extent that we're finding people aren't using it, we want to address that too," she said. KIRKLAND TIGHTENS LID ON FINANCES Kirkland & Ellis, the highest-grossing US law firm, said it will no longer report its annual financial results to The American Lawyer. The firm, whose revenue topped $10 billion last year, said in a Wednesday letter to editors at the legal trade publication that "public reporting of our revenue and profits does not provide meaningful value to our clients nor adequately reflect the caliber of our firm’s legal services." It said publicizing its finances for ranking purposes "could incentivize quantitative metrics over qualitative strengths," like the quality of its legal services, according to the letter, which was viewed by Reuters. The American Lawyer annually publishes lists of the 200 highest-grossing and most profitable law firms in the country. Kirkland, driven in part by its private equity and restructuring work, has topped the revenue rankings since 2017. Kirkland's revenue hit $10.56 billion in 2025, while its average profits per equity partner reached $11.1 million. The firm has a tiered partnership in which a substantial number of partners do not have a traditional ownership stake. Also on Billable Hours' radar this week... --AT&T's legal department has stopped paying law firms to handle many routine assignments typically done by junior lawyers, and is instead using an in-house team using AI, Reuters columnist Sara Randazzo [USN:L6N45S1A5 TEXT:"reports"]. AT&T's general counsel said its roster of 30 or so outside law firms could shrink in the future. --President Donald Trump’s administration is vying in federal court to allow the EEOC to keep information secret from the public about its probes last year targeting the employment practices at some major US law firms. The [USN:L6N45S09L TEXT:"administration is contesting"] a lawsuit over access to the records, and says a significant amount of information must remain confidential. --Cornell University has [USN:L6N45S15B TEXT:"hired Sally Yates"], who served as deputy US attorney general from 2015 to 2017, for an internal investigation of how it handled a student's allegations that she was gang-raped, a case that has brought mounting scrutiny and triggered student protests at the Ivy League school. Read more: [USN:L6N45K07C TEXT:"Thousands of web-tracking lawsuits face extinction under California overhaul"] [USN:L6N45D0X6 TEXT:"Law firms vie for tech talent in AI race"] [USN:L6N42308A TEXT:"AI error-ridden court filings surge despite three years of sanctions"]

item.title: Amid frontline advances, Ukraine’s cities face up to lack of air defence
item.description: As Ukraine's capital came under some of the heaviest direct bombardment of the war last week, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy met a delegation of Japanese members of parliament and then German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
item.dc:creator: Peter Apps
item.content:encoded: As Ukraine's capital came under some of the heaviest direct bombardment of the war last week, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy met a delegation of Japanese members of parliament and then German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. While the Japanese parliamentarians visited an underground drone workshop in the capital, Merz attended a memorial to slain Ukrainian service personnel as well as the scene of a Russian strike on the National Academy of Sciences in late September. Before Merz headed back to Berlin, the leaders announced that, despite warnings from the Kremlin for foreign embassies to quit the Ukrainian capital for safety, neither Germany nor any other major nation had any plans to do so. Still, with a lack of air defences now leaving Kyiv and other major cities wide open to attack, and summer's warmth coming to an end, Ukrainians themselves are now bracing for perhaps the toughest winter of the 4-1/2-year-old war. "Protection against all of this is the number one priority for me and Ukraine," Zelenskiy said, saying that Russian reverses on the eastern front were pushing a furious Kremlin towards throwing ever greater resources into its aerial onslaught. UKRAINE MAKES SOME PROGRESS ON THE BATTLEFIELD When it comes to fighting on the ground, Ukraine has indeed had a good few weeks. Last week saw social media footage of heavily shielded “Turtle” tanks – covered in extensive steel cages and shielding to protect themselves from drone attack – advancing on a battlefield in eastern Ukraine under the protection of numerous Ukrainian aerial drones. Elsewhere on the front, in the eastern region of Donetsk, Ukrainian media reported their forces had steered several Soviet-era armoured personnel carriers by remote control as giant rolling bombs to break through heavily defended Russian positions. Other commanders talked of drones airlifting smaller, unmanned ground vehicles forward for a robot-led assault. The frontline continues to evolve: while some video footage from the front showed small groups of Ukrainian soldiers advancing in person, survival in open areas is now all but impossible. Speaking at the London Resilience Summit this week, veterans of several Ukrainian frontline units said both sides were now increasingly also digging tunnels and beginning to design new drones to do so. “It’s like something from 1916,” one said, comparing it to the tunnelling battles of the First World War. On October 1, President Vladimir Putin said Russian forces had seized more than 1,300 sq km (500 sq miles) of territory in September. According to analysis conducted by the Washington-based Institute for the Study of War, however, Russia suffered a net territorial loss of 80 sq km (31 sq miles). Ukraine's counteroffensive – Operation Vivaldi – focusing on the Lyman region has yielded significant successes. Atlantic Council analyst David Kirichenko described it as reversing a full year's worth of Russian gains, significantly reducing the risk of further Russian breakthroughs against Ukraine’s eastern “fortress belt” in the coming months. In addition to a continuing campaign of strikes on Russian refineries, which has triggered fuel shortages and reduced export revenue, Ukraine also continues to strike infrastructure, including, recently a datacentre owned by Internet giant Yandex. RUSSIAN BARRAGE LOOKS OMINOUS FOR WINTER The bigger picture, though, looks harsher for Ukraine. An ever-growing volume of Russian ballistic missiles and a sophisticated new generation of Shahed drones are now penetrating Ukraine’s capital and essential infrastructure, raising the prospect of yet another, perhaps more severe, winter struggle for heat and power. Ukraine says it was hit by 900 Shaheds last week alone, with targets including bridges across the river that divides Kyiv in two. Meanwhile European and other Western weapons systems are reaching Ukraine more slowly than had been hoped. Most critical are the air defence missiles that Ukraine has, in essence, run out of. Talks with the US at NATO’s Ankara summit in July about providing Patriot missiles directly to Ukraine rather than from allies' stocks have yielded little. And while European nations are working together to produce the Ukrainian-designed Freya, there seems little prospect of it entering service before 2027. Meanwhile, Ukrainian officials said last month, Russia is now producing 140 ballistic missiles a month – many of which are launched almost immediately to inflict destruction while Ukraine has little answer to them. Ukraine has received donations of F-16 fast jets from its Western allies, but says many are now back in western Europe for repairs, grounded by a lack of engine parts. On the other hand, it is having more success fending off Russia's new, jet-powered Shahed drones. Ihor Klymenko, secretary of Ukraine's National Security and Defence Council, said 82% of incoming jet drones had been downed on Wednesday night, although others, and other missiles, reached their targets. NOT ALL WESTERN AID IS USEFUL TO UKRAINE While European defence tech executives continue to visit Kyiv with its bomb shelter hotels and elite life continuing under the bombardment, Ukraine was last month forced to cancel its “Brave One” arms fair in the western city of Lviv. Western defence firms continue to seek out Ukrainian military partners to field-test their latest weaponry, among them drones with saws to sever the fibre-optic control cables many Russian drones use. Yet some Ukrainian personnel say the quality is extremely mixed. “Sometimes there are a lot of buzzwords," said one operator. "We can be really overwhelmed with all the offers to test and validate technology – but that can be useless without the tactics.” High on the list of Ukraine's requirements, they said, is drone weaponry that can penetrate and destroy Russian bunkers under the front lines. Russia, too, keeps innovating: UK Defence Intelligence last week described what it believed was the first engagement between Russian and Ukrainian drone vessels in the Black Sea. It is also signalling steady resolve. Last week Russia concluded its massive “Centre” military drills along the Caspian Sea, a 47,000- personnel simulated seizure of hostile territory that included displays of Russia’s own new unmanned ground vehicles as well as its first autonomous tanks. Last weekend, at least five drones and missiles penetrated the airspace of Ukraine’s neighbour Moldova, described by both the Ukrainian and Moldovan governments as a deliberate act. Governments have also blamed Russia for a steadily rising number of [USN:L8N45121N TEXT:"sabotage incidents"] in Europe - an allegation Moscow rejects. This winter that is likely to continue or worsen; few in Ukraine or Eastern Europe hold out much hope for US-brokered talks reaching any kind of breakthrough.

item.title: USA Today processa OpenAI por violação de direitos autorais
item.description: A USA Today Co e vários jornais que controla entraram com uma ação contra a OpenAI no tribunal federal de Manhattan nesta quinta-feira, acusando a companhia de inteligência artificial de infringir direitos autorais ao usar seu conteúdo para treinar modelos de IA.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: A USA Today Co (TDAY.N) e vários jornais que controla entraram com uma ação contra a OpenAI no tribunal federal de Manhattan nesta quinta-feira, acusando a companhia de inteligência artificial de infringir direitos autorais ao usar seu conteúdo para treinar modelos de IA. A ação judicial alega que a OpenAI copiou centenas de milhares de textos e outros materiais desses veículos de comunicação e os utilizou sem permissão para treinar o sistema por trás do chatbot ChatGPT. Porta-vozes da OpenAI não responderam imediatamente a um pedido de comentário sobre a ação. O processo do USA Today é um de dezenas abertos por detentores de direitos autorais contra empresas de tecnologia, incluindo OpenAI, Anthropic e Meta, por uso de conteúdo em treinamento de IA. As empresas de tecnologia argumentam que seus sistemas fazem uso justo de material protegido por direitos autorais, transformando-o em algo novo. A OpenAI e seu maior financiador, a Microsoft (MSFT.O) , enfrentam ações semelhantes no tribunal de Manhattan movidas por autores e veículos de notícias importantes, incluindo o New York Times (NYT.N) . O USA Today cobra indenização “superior a US$ 250 milhões” e uma ordem judicial bloqueando o uso de seu contéudo pela OpenAI.

item.title: Australia skipper nonplussed over forthcoming book that might add to Sandpapergate fallout
item.description: Australia’s 2018 ball-tampering scandal is back in the spotlight as the test side return to South Africa for the first time since “Sandpapergate”, but captain Pat Cummins on Thursday dismissed suggestions that Usman Khawaja’s autobiography could trigger further fallout when it is published next month.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gleeson
item.content:encoded: Australia’s 2018 ball-tampering scandal is back in the spotlight as the test side return to South Africa for the first time since “Sandpapergate”, but captain Pat Cummins on Thursday dismissed suggestions that Usman Khawaja’s autobiography could trigger further fallout when it is published next month. Australia’s 33-year-old test skipper was one of the bowlers who played in the March 2018 test at Cape Town where Australia were caught using sandpaper to scuff up one side of the ball in an illegal effort to produce prodigious swing. It sparked a major crisis for Cricket Australia, but only captain Steve Smith and batsmen David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, who was caught with the sandpaper in his pocket, were banned for their part in the scandal. The bowling quartet of Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied any knowledge of the incident. All four are back in South Africa for the three-test series, the first in South Africa since the scandal, which starts at Kingsmead on Friday. Cummins confirmed he has spoken with Khawaja, who was also in the Australian team at Newlands eight years ago. “Didn't go back into too much detail. He just basically gave me the heads-up that he's doing a book, and yeah, as always, no worries. Tell your story. It's fine,” Cummins said. Australian media have reported that Khawaja had urged the team to take collective responsibility at the time of the scandal but the suggestion had been shot down. Cummins said he did not know about the contents of the book. “You need to ask him,” he said. “It’s obviously a long time ago. All the investigations, everything was done back then. Answered every question a million times. So, yeah, it was dealt with then. Now all I can say is, as a group, we moved on, very happy with the last eight years, how we’ve been as a group and evolved.” South African broadcaster SuperSport, whose cameras caught the offending Australians, has poked some fun at the 2018 scandal with a clip on social media that shows Bancroft using the sandpaper on the ball and Australia's reaction after being caught red-handed eight years ago. In the social media post , the broadcaster warned: “Our cameras will be sharp for this 3-match test series.” (This story has been refiled to remove the extraneous word 'the' in paragraph 11.)

item.title: Hurricane Isaias strengthens as US Gulf Coast prepares for landfall
item.description: Hurricane Isaias strengthened on Thursday as it barreled toward the US Gulf Coast, prompting mandatory evacuations in parts of Florida and emergency declarations in Alabama as forecasters warned of life-threatening storm surges, tornadoes and flooding.
item.dc:creator: Brad Brooks
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Isaias strengthened on Thursday as it barreled toward the US Gulf Coast, prompting mandatory evacuations in parts of Florida and emergency declarations in Alabama as forecasters warned of life-threatening storm surges, tornadoes and flooding. Isaias has already disrupted oil and gas production in the Gulf of Mexico, forcing energy companies to evacuate offshore platforms and shut down operations. The first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season was packing maximum sustained winds of 85 mph (140 kph) early on Thursday, the US National Hurricane Center said. Isaias was forecast to strengthen to near Category 3 intensity, with sustained winds reaching 110 mph (175 kph) on Friday before reaching the northern Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday. "We are expecting Isaias to be a dangerous hurricane when it makes landfall,” NHC director Michael Brennan said in a Thursday morning briefing. "Today is the day to prepare and get ready." Isaias nearly tied the record for the latest first Atlantic hurricane with one that hit on October 8, 1905. The strong El Nino weather pattern this year has suppressed Atlantic hurricane development by increasing vertical wind shear, which disrupts the formation of strengthening tropical storms. The hurricane was moving east-northeast at 10 mph (17 kph), about 380 miles (610 km) south of the mouth of the Mississippi River at 7 a.m. US Central time, the NHC said. IMPACTS ON OIL, GAS Isaias is expected to pass through areas with significant offshore [USN:L1N45T0JO TEXT:"oil and gas production"], along with onshore refining facilities, which could pressure inventories and already-high prices at the pump. US energy companies such as Shell (SHEL.L) and Chevron (CVX.N) [USN:L4N45T1Q7 TEXT:"said"] they were curtailing offshore operations at their Gulf platforms. US Gulf of Mexico oil and gas producers had shut in about 25.08% of current oil production and 16.37% of current natural gas production as of Wednesday, according to the Marine Minerals Administration. WARNINGS, STORM SURGE Hurricane warnings stretched from coastal Mississippi through Alabama to the Florida panhandle, while tropical-storm and storm-surge warnings extended into southeastern Louisiana, the NHC said. Forecasters warned that storm surges could reach 5 to 7 feet (1.5 to 2.1 meters) above sea level in the hardest-hit coastal areas, with rainfall of 3 to 7 inches (8 to 18 cm) and isolated totals of 10 inches (25 cm). The hurricane was forecast to reach sustained winds of around 110 mph (175 kph) early Friday before weakening somewhat as it approached land. Increasing vertical wind shear, which can disrupt a hurricane's circulation, was expected to limit its strength near landfall, though forecasters warned it would remain dangerous. EVACUATIONS ORDERED In Florida, officials ordered mandatory evacuations beginning at noon local time on Thursday for coastal areas of Okaloosa County. The county urged tourists to leave the area and announced plans to close three airports Thursday evening. Governor Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency in 25 Florida counties earlier in the week. Alabama Governor Kay Ivey declared a state of emergency covering 40 counties, while officials on Dauphin Island issued an evacuation notice for the western portion of the barrier island beginning Thursday evening. Baldwin County, Alabama, encouraged residents of low-lying coastal areas to evacuate voluntarily and prepared emergency shelters. In Mississippi, Jackson County and the city of Gautier declared local emergencies as coastal communities prepared for flooding and power outages.

item.title: US House Speaker Johnson weighs 'next chapter' if Republicans lose majority-Fox News
item.description: Republican US House of Representatives Speaker Mike Johnson told Fox News he does not know if he will remain in politics if his party loses control of the chamber in next month's congressional election even as he insisted his focus was on protecting the party's majority.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Republican US House of Representatives Speaker Mike Johnson told Fox News he does not know if he will remain in politics if his party loses control of the chamber in next month's congressional election even as he insisted his focus was on protecting the party's majority. "Heaven forbid, if we lose this majority or whatever, I don't know what my next chapter of life is,” the Louisiana lawmaker told Fox News. Johnson has repeatedly predicted that Republicans would defy history and grow their House majority in the upcoming election. But he has on occasion held out the possibility of a Republican loss in efforts to raise money and turnout, predicting that a Democratic majority would mean another Trump impeachment. The latest comments appeared to be his public acknowledgment that his caucus could face defeat in November. "If God moves on our hearts and says we should, you know, go back to my hometown of Shreveport and start a lawn business, I'll do that with equal fervor. I mean, I just want to be of my highest and best use ... to God and to my country,” Johnson said, Fox News reporter Aishah Hasnie said on X. His comments come as US voters are already heading to the polls in a number of states to vote early ahead of the November 3 election day, with rising prices and the Iran war looming large as [USN:L1N44V0PF TEXT:"Americans weigh"] Republicans' grip on Congress and fellow Republican Donald Trump in the White House. Reuters/Ipsos polling shows 44% of registered voters saying they would vote for Democrats while 37% say they would vote for Republicans and 13% undecided. Nearly two-thirds of US adults nationwide, or 65%, said they disapprove of Trump's term since taking office for a second time in January 2025, compared to 32% who said they approve. Johnson said he was not to blame if Republicans lose their legislative majority, telling Fox: "If we lose the House, it will be because the people were misled." "I'm traveling nonstop,” added Johnson, who scheduled the House to be in recess until after the election. Trump has also [USN:L1N45L12S TEXT:"begun campaign-trail rallies"].

item.title: Incerteza eleitoral amplia preocupações sobre futuro da agenda climática brasileira
item.description: A eleição presidencial apertada tem deixado investidores, empresas e executivos ligados à agenda climática preocupados diante da possibilidade de um eventual governo liderado pelo senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) não manter as políticas que sustentam a emergente economia verde do Brasil.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Araujo, Marcela Ayres
item.content:encoded: A eleição presidencial apertada tem deixado investidores, empresas e executivos ligados à agenda climática preocupados diante da possibilidade de um eventual governo liderado pelo senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) não manter as políticas que sustentam a emergente economia verde do Brasil. Flávio liderou o primeiro turno das eleições no fim de semana com um desempenho melhor do que o esperado, após uma campanha na qual prometeu fortalecer o mercado regulamentado de carbono, mas evitou criticar o histórico climático de seu pai, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, em cujo governo o desmatamento disparou. No segundo turno, em 25 de outubro, ele enfrentará o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, que tem buscado posicionar o Brasil como um polo de financiamento climático, lançando programas para atrair capital privado para projetos verdes e estabelecendo as bases para um mercado de carbono regulamentado. O setor industrial pressionou Bolsonaro para que não abandonasse essas iniciativas, dados os potenciais custos para a economia. "Seria uma burrice econômica você retroagir nessa agenda", disse Tereza Campello, diretora socioambiental do banco estatal de desenvolvimento BNDES. Embora a campanha de Flávio também tenha prometido expandir a bioeconomia, com foco em produtos farmacêuticos e cosméticos, investidores e executivos ainda manifestam preocupações com suas declarações anteriores a respeito das mudanças climáticas. Em entrevista concedida à TV Globo em agosto, Flávio descreveu os eventos climáticos extremos como cíclicos e afirmou não acreditar que sejam causados exclusivamente pela ação humana. Ele declarou que a melhor maneira de lidar com as preocupações climáticas seria por meio de investimentos em saneamento básico. O plano de governo do senador ignorou em grande parte as metas de redução de emissões de gases causadores do efeito estufa, de acordo com o Observatório do Clima. "Nota-se que propostas como o combate ao desmatamento ou o reforço do poder de fiscalização dos órgãos de proteção ambiental são flagrantemente incompatíveis com a prática de seu mandato no Senado", afirmou o grupo. A campanha de Flávio disse que a agenda ambiental do senador, no caso de vitória na eleição, seria aprimorada durante o período de transição entre governos, sem responder diretamente se as iniciativas de financiamento verde de Lula seriam mantidas. Flávio priorizaria incentivos de conservação baseados no mercado, como o pagamento por serviços ambientais, e o fortalecimento dos esforços para combater crimes ambientais, numa tentativa de eliminar o desmatamento ilegal até 2029, um ano antes da meta de Lula, segundo a campanha. BENEFÍCIOS ECONÔMICOS Durante o governo de Jair Bolsonaro, entre 2019 e 2022, as proteções ambientais foram enfraquecidas e o desmatamento se expandiu pela Amazônia brasileira. Desde então, o governo Lula tem incentivado a indústria brasileira de remoção de carbono por meio de empréstimos e investimentos do BNDES. Durante sua campanha, o presidente prometeu expandir instrumentos de financiamento climático como o Eco Invest, que mobilizou R$190 bilhões desde 2024. Especialistas do setor afirmam que os benefícios econômicos da agenda climática do Brasil são difíceis de ignorar. "A agenda climática e a visão do governo dessa indústria como sendo superestratégica no país não depende de partido", disse Gabriel Silva, diretor executivo da startup de remoção de carbono Mombak. Independentemente de quem vencer as eleições, Silva disse esperar continuidade, em parte devido ao desenvolvimento do mercado regulamentado de carbono no Brasil e às opções de crédito oferecidas pelo BNDES. Hoje, créditos de carbono brasileiros são negociados no mercado voluntário por empresas com metas próprias de redução de emissões. Com a regulamentação aprovada em 2024, o país se prepara para lançar um mercado regulado, permitindo que empresas usem créditos para cumprir metas obrigatórias de descarbonização e abrindo espaço para sua negociação internacional. DIFÍCIL DE REVERTER O apoio das empresas ao programa também poderia encorajar Flávio a mantê-lo. Antes do primeiro turno da eleição, o Conselho Empresarial Brasileiro para o Desenvolvimento Sustentável (CEBDS), cujos membros incluem a Petrobras (PETR3.SA) e a Vale (VALE3.SA) , disse aos candidatos que considera o mercado regulamentado de carbono uma questão fundamental para a economia do país. "Em 2025, cerca de US$2,2 trilhões foram investidos globalmente em tecnologias de energia limpa. Esse capital é móvel", disse Daniela Mignani, diretora executiva de gestão corporativa do CEBDS, acrescentando que os investidores podem migrar para outros lugares diante da incerteza regulatória. Campello, do BNDES, afirmou que a lógica econômica por trás da agenda climática de Lula pode dificultar sua reversão, dada a crescente demanda por produtos da bioeconomia, incluindo madeira certificada, bem como cacau e café cultivados em áreas reflorestadas. O programa florestal do BNDES disponibilizou cerca de R$15 bilhões em empréstimos e investimentos para projetos voltados à recuperação e proteção de florestas locais.

item.title: Cowboys activate LG Tyler Smith from IR
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys activated three-time Pro Bowl guard Tyler Smith from injured reserve prior to Thursday's game against the visiting Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Dallas Cowboys activated three-time Pro Bowl guard Tyler Smith from injured reserve prior to Thursday's game against the visiting Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Smith underwent surgery to repair a ligament in his thumb during training camp. The Cowboys (2-2) opened the 21-day practice window on Monday for Smith, who was listed as questionable to face the Buccaneers (0-4). T.J. Bass had played at left guard in place of Smith. Smith, 25, has started 63 regular-season games. Dallas selected him No. 24 overall in the 2022 NFL Draft. He has been named to the Pro Bowl in each of the last three seasons. Also, the Cowboys waived running back Emari Demercado and elevated cornerback Reddy Steward and safety Juanyeh Thomas from the practice squad for Thursday's game. Demercado, 27, had five carries for 15 yards while playing in two games this season for Dallas. He had been inactive with fellow running back Tyler Goodson serving as Javonte Williams' backup. The Cowboys claimed Demercado off waivers on Sept. 1. --Field Level Media

Oct 8 : Revolut would favor a primary listing in the United States if the digital bank decides to pursue an initial pubic offering in the future, CEO Nik Storonsky told Bloomberg TV on Thursday. Storonsky, who founded Revolut, told Bloomberg TV that the firm wants to "dominate" the US market and plans to roll out credit cards and loans, once it receives a full banking charter. Revolut received preliminary approval for a national banking licence in the United States in September, after getting licences in Britain and France earlier this year. The bank has risen to become Europe's most valuable startup, having grown rapidly since it was launched just over a decade ago as a fintech promising cheaper forex fees. Valued at $115 billion privately, Revolut is now worth more than Britain's Barclays  and France's Societe Generale. The company's top boss had previously told French newspaper Les Echos the bank was looking into a dual stock market listing in New York and London. Any eventual listing is still likely to be at least a year away, with past media reports citing 2028, and subject to market conditions.

item.title: US imposes fresh sanctions on Iran's shadow fleet
item.description: The US imposed fresh sanctions on Iran on Thursday, targeting individuals, networks and 17 vessels for transporting Iranian crude, oil products and petrochemicals, the Treasury Department said, as Washington stepped up economic pressure on Tehran.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Gardner, Daphne Psaledakis
item.content:encoded: The US imposed fresh sanctions on Iran on Thursday, targeting individuals, networks and 17 vessels for transporting Iranian crude, oil products and petrochemicals, the Treasury Department said, as Washington stepped up economic pressure on Tehran. The sanctions are part of the department's "Operation Economic Outcast," which aims to cut Iran's funding for the war with the US, missile construction, cyberattacks and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, or IRGC. "Today's action represents the most significant blow yet to Iran's remaining illicit maritime infrastructure by neutralizing the vast majority of the shadow fleet," a Treasury official told reporters on a call. "Treasury is cutting off the regime's last major source of illicit revenue and strengthening international pressure to hold Tehran accountable." The move tightens the squeeze on Iranian oil sales after the US reimposed its blockade of Iranian ports on July 14 following the breakdown of a memorandum of understanding between Tehran and Washington to end the war. Iran has only about 20 million barrels of crude oil left on vessels outside the blockade, off Singapore , Malaysia and China , the Treasury official said. The world uses about 100 million barrels of oil per day. A second Treasury official said Iran has stopped loading and offloading crude oil vessels due to the blockade and sanctions. President Donald Trump said on social media on Thursday that the US is having "productive discussions" with Iran over the war that began on February 28. Trump said the US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections on November 3. An analyst said the fact that the US is sanctioning vessels after Iran has delivered virtually all of its oil at sea means the impact will be muted. "This is economic warfare conducted in the rearview mirror, designed to generate headlines rather than results," said Brett Erickson, a managing principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors. Vessels targeted by the US sanctions include the Comoros-flagged Paritosh, the Panama-flagged Bitu and the Bahamas-flagged Gas Lucky.

Oct 8 : Everton forward Martin Sherif has been fined £5,000 ($6,600) after admitting to breaches of the Football Association's betting regulations over a 15-month period, the FA said on Thursday. The 20-year-old, who is yet to make a senior appearance for the Premier League club, admitted responsibility for 61 bets being placed on soccer matches between November 20, 2024 and February 12, 2026. "The player admitted breaching FA Rule E1.2 by causing, permitting, or enabling 61 bets to be placed on football matches," the FA said in a statement. In mitigation, Sherif maintained he had not personally placed any of the wagers.

[８日　ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のウォーシュ議長は、タイのバンコクで今月１６日に開催される国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）年次総会で講演を行う。ＩＭＦの日程表から明らかになった。２７─２８日に開かれる連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）を控え、ＦＲＢ当局者が対外発言を控える「ブラックアウト」期間入り前の最後の日となる。

item.title: Steelers WR Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) to miss multiple games
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. will not have a reunion on the field versus his former team.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. will not have a reunion on the field versus his former team. Pittman, in fact, will be sidelined for longer than just Sunday's game against the visiting Indianapolis Colts. Head coach Mike McCarthy said Thursday that Pittman will sit out multiple games after re-injuring his left foot. "It's the same foot, so it's going to be a multiple-week injury," McCarthy said. "We're still going through the evaluation of his roster position." Pittman, 29, has just seven catches for 89 yards in three games (all starts) since he signed a three-year, $59 million contract extension. He was traded by the Colts in March along with a seventh-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft to the Steelers for a sixth-round selection in the same draft. Pittman caught 80 passes for 784 yards and a career-high seven touchdowns in 17 games (16 starts) with Indianapolis in 2025. He posted two 1,000-yard seasons with the Colts despite considerable turnover at quarterback since he was drafted 34th overall in 2020. He has caught 492 passes for 5,343 yards and 25 TDs in 98 career games (89 starts). Also on Thursday, the Steelers opened the 21-day practice window for safety DeShon Elliott. Elliott was placed on the injured reserve on Aug. 30 as he continued to recover from knee and hamstring injuries that limited his 2025 season. Elliott, 29, recorded 38 tackles, an interception, a sack and a forced fumble in five games (all starts) last season. He has totaled 433 tackles, five interceptions and 4.5 sacks in 77 career games (69 starts) with the Baltimore Ravens, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins and Steelers. --Field Level Media

item.description:
Olivia Le Poidevin
[ジュネーブ ８日 ロイター] - 世界貿易機関（ＷＴＯ）は８日、世界のモノ（財...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＷＴＯ、26年モノの貿易量3.9％増に上方修正　ＡＩ需要が押し上げ 1:49 配信

2026年7月17日、米国カリフォルニア州ロングビーチ港で撮影。REUTERS/Mario Anzuoni/File Photo

Olivia Le Poidevin

[ジュネーブ ８日 ロイター] - 世界貿易機関（ＷＴＯ）は８日、世界のモノ（財）の貿易量の２０２６年の伸び率見通しを３．９％とし、３月時点の予想１．９％から引き上げた。中東情勢による混乱の影響はあるものの、半導体やデータセンターなど人工知能（ＡＩ）関連製品への需要が伸びる見通し。２７年の伸び率予想は４．１％に上方修正した。一方、燃料や肥料の価格高騰を受けた家計の購買力低下や、ＡＩの投資ブームに減速リスクがあると指摘した。

地域別では、アジアは輸入が９．５％、輸出が９．９％、それぞれ増える見通し。アフリカも輸入が８．９％、輸出が５．６％増えると見込んだ。中東は輸出入ともに大幅減となる見通しだ。

２６年１─６月期のモノの貿易量が前年同期比３．５％増だったのに対し、ドル建ての貿易額は１５％増えた。エネルギー価格高騰や、ＡＩ関連製品への需要を反映しており、貿易額の増加分の４７％をＡＩ関連商品が占めた。

２６年の世界の国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）は２．６％増と予測。地域別ではアジアが４．３％増と最も高い伸びとなり、アフリカ、南米が続くと見込んだ。

２６年のサービス貿易の伸び率の見通しは、従来予想の４．８％から３．３％に引き下げた。航空燃料費の高騰が響くものの、２７年は６．４％に回復すると予想した。

Oct 8 : Southampton manager Tonda Eckert said he had accepted responsibility for his role in the club's "spygate" scandal and welcomed the clarity provided by the verdict ahead of Sunday’s south-coast derby against Portsmouth. Eckert was handed a suspended six-week ban and a £28,000 ($36,979) fine after admitting he authorised the observation of training sessions of three rival Championship clubs last season. The FA charged Eckert in July and an independent regulatory commission imposed the sanctions following a hearing, with the governing body confirming on Wednesday that the ban would remain suspended until the end of the 2027-28 season. "I made a mistake and I said that relatively quickly and then I think you just have to accept the consequences," Eckert told reporters on Thursday.

"And that's not just for me, that's for everyone involved in this football club." Eckert acknowledged that he could have faced a much heavier punishment and said the decision allowed Southampton to draw a line under the affair. "There was a fair chance that the verdict goes a different way. After such a long time, we've had a verdict from the EFL, we've had a verdict now (from the FA). "Whatever you expect is not necessarily what you get in the end, so for me it's to hold my hand up one more time." Southampton were expelled from last season's Championship playoff final and deducted four points for the 2026-27 campaign after observing Oxford United, Ipswich Town and Middlesbrough in training. item.title: South African anti-migrant protests turn violent, government blames disinformation
item.description: Anti-migrant protests in two South African cities including Johannesburg's Soweto township turned violent on Thursday, with the government blaming disinformation over a court ruling on asylum seekers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anti-migrant protests in two South African cities including Johannesburg's Soweto township turned violent on Thursday, with the government blaming disinformation over a court ruling on asylum seekers. In coastal Durban, the second city hit by protests, a Reuters reporter saw five cars in flames in the urban centre, where foreign-owned shops were also looted. The unrest followed a protest by a group demanding that a refugee centre stop processing asylum applications. In Soweto, a Reuters reporter saw residents carrying groceries out of a shop that they said was owned by a person from Somalia, whom they chased away. The looters fled after police arrived and made them disperse. Government spokesperson William Baloyi said the violence was triggered by people spreading deliberately false information about a constitutional court ruling in July. The country's highest court ruled that asylum seekers cannot be denied access to South Africa's asylum system solely for procedural reasons such as having entered the country illegally. Baloyi said the ruling had been widely misrepresented and did not automatically grant refugee status, permanent residence or other legal rights to undocumented migrants. "We are deeply concerned by what is going on now," he added. Police said in a statement that they had mobilised more officers in Durban, where they said at least 14 vehicles had been set alight while a guest house and warehouse were partially burned. A top police official, Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane, planned to hold a press conference in Soweto on efforts to maintain law and order there. South Africa has seen months of [USN:L1N43205U TEXT:"anti-migrant marches"] this year that have drawn international criticism. Some of the marches have descended into violence and looting, and thousands of African foreign nationals have fled the country. Migrants are often blamed for taking jobs, fuelling crime and straining public services, claims that social scientists say are not supported by evidence. Three decades since apartheid ended, South Africa remains deeply unequal and about a third of people are out of work. Despite this, it remains Africa's largest economy and continues to draw migrants.

item.title: 米、11月中間選挙前にイラン攻撃せず＝トランプ氏
item.description: [ワシントン ８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター

[ワシントン ８日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は８日、米国がイランと「建設的な」協議を行っているとした上で、１１月の米中間選挙前にイランへの攻撃は実施しないとの考えを表明した。

トランプ大統領は自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」への投稿で、イランと協議を行っていると述べると同時に、イランの港湾に対する米国の封鎖は依然として有効であり、石油はホルムズ海峡を通って輸送されていると強調した。

その上で「われわれは１１月３日に米国で行われる中間選挙まで、いかなる時点においてもイランを攻撃することはない」と言明した。

MOSCOW, Oct 8 : Russian technology and AI company Yandex said on Thursday it could not yet determine whether equipment at a data centre hit by a Ukrainian drone attack could be restored. Yandex said earlier that the attack on its Sasovo hub, one of its five large data centres, caused a fire and forced it to suspend operations at the site, which hosts tens of thousands of servers. "The scale of the damage to the infrastructure is still being assessed," Yandex said in a statement. "For the moment, we cannot confirm whether it is possible to restore the data centre equipment in Sasovo." The company earlier said some of its services were unavailable and specialist teams were at the site assessing the damage. Two of Yandex's three supercomputers, used to develop its AI model, are housed at the Sasovo data centre. Yandex has not said whether they were damaged.

Source: Reuters

item.title: イラン、ウラン濃縮活動放棄せず 保有ウラン引き渡しも拒否＝原子力庁長官
item.description: [ドバイ ８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ドバイ　８日　ロイター] - イランのエスラミ原子力庁長官は８日、米国がイランに対しウラン濃縮能力の「意味のある」削減を求めたことを受け、イランはウラン濃縮活動を放棄せず、保有するウランを引き渡すこともないと述べた。国営メディアが報じた。

エスラミ長官は、米国が改めてイランの核施設への攻撃を示唆したことについて「目新しいものではない」とした上で、「ウラン濃縮は核プロセスの不可欠な一部で、われわれはいかなる形でもこれを放棄しない」とし、「核産業は科学技術発展の原動力だ。プロセスの出発点を持たずして、どうやって核産業を有すると主張できるのか」と述べた。

イスラエルや米国など西側諸国はイランが核兵器開発を目指していると非難しており、民生利用に必要な水準を大きく上回る６０％へのウラン濃縮を根拠の一つに挙げている。イランはこれを否定しているが、高濃縮ウランの濃度引き下げには応じる可能性を示している。

FAST

LONDON, Oct 8 : The National Basketball Association and International Basketball Federation (FIBA) say they remain committed to building a league in Europe despite the Euroleague having turned down their collaboration offer at a shareholders' assembly on Tuesday. The future of European basketball is in the balance, with the NBA saying it is keen to move forward with its NBA Europe project in 2027 whether a deal is reached or not. The current premier competition in European basketball, the Euroleague, has said it is open to collaborating with the NBA but voted on Tuesday against accepting an NBA proposal. With the Euroleague pressing ahead with its own expansion project, the window is narrowing on any deal before the European basketball landscape shifts. If no deal is found, NBA Europe and the Euroleague would enter direct competition.

“A partnership between the Euroleague, FIBA and the NBA to unify the European basketball ecosystem would unlock the game’s enormous potential across Europe," said a joint statement from the NBA and FIBA on Thursday. "The NBA and FIBA remain committed to moving forward with a new professional men’s league in Europe and helping build a stronger, more sustainable basketball ecosystem alongside partners who share our vision of growth, opportunity and the core principles of the European sports model." Speaking later on Thursday at the Leaders Week sports industry conference in London, NBA Europe Director George Aivazoglou confirmed that they were "moving ahead with plans for a launch next year."  "We're very serious and consistent in terms of our intention to work with everybody who shares our vision of the future," Aivazoglou said. Aivazoglou also confirmed that their league would start with 16 teams, adding it would reward teams through qualification on sporting merit more than the Euroleague setup. He expressed doubts about the current format of European basketball. "There is a serious value gap for European basketball. We don't think it's reaching its potential. And we have a perspective about what has happened and what needs to happen to move things forward." A senior executive at a Euroleague club told Reuters on Thursday that he expected the NBA to come back with an improved offer. The executive added that the 13 Euroleague shareholder clubs are committed to taking any decision together. Talks between the NBA and Euroleague regarding a deal could continue but there is no deadline for an agreement to be reached. A senior sports executive told Reuters on Tuesday that any collaboration was unlikely to begin before 2028. A person attending the Euroleague shareholders' assembly on Tuesday told Reuters they will meet again within a month to decide on the allocation of long-term Euroleague licences.

Source: Reuters

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 8 : Manchester City striker Erling Haaland urged the embattled club's supporters to stick together in his first public comments since City were found guilty of more than 100 charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules. City have appealed against the independent commission’s verdict, insisting the judgment contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact." Asked what his message was to supporters ahead of what should be a combustible Premier League match at Liverpool on Sunday, Haaland called for unity and positivity amid the off-field turmoil. "We have to stick together. We have to stay with each other, and we have to stay positive," the Norway striker told Sky Sports. "No matter what happens in life, we always have to have a smile.

"So we have to stay positive, look ahead, and try to win football games and try to enjoy the situation and win the game. "We have to stick together; we have to spread the love to each other. So yeah: stick together, and enjoy the ride and smile." The independent commission found that City arranged "sham" contracts with several commercial partners as part of what it described as a "disguised funding scheme" that artificially inflated the club's revenues and reduced its costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.19 billion). The charges spanned nearly a decade. Haaland, whose father Alf-Inge also played for City, said his connection to the club and the UK in general extended beyond playing for Enzo Maresca's side. "I care a lot about this place, and the UK generally, I care a lot about the fans because I'm a fan myself, and I feel with them as well," he said. City take a three-point lead atop the table to Anfield on Sunday to face opponents with whom they developed a fierce rivalry during Pep Guardiola's battles with former Liverpool manager Juergen Klopp. "It's always special to play against Liverpool," Haaland said. "Especially with Pep and Klopp. I remember sitting and watching the games (before signing with City), how much they pushed each other. It's always special games there. "I won there, I drew there, I lost. So it's always special, and every Premier League game is different, and every game against Liverpool is always special." ($1 = 0.7571 pounds)

Oct 8 : Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka has received a suspended fine of 150,000 Swiss francs ($180,159) after admitting he obtained a fake COVID-19 vaccination certificate, the midfielder said on social media on Thursday. The fine comprises 50 daily penalties of 3,000 francs and will not be enforced provided Xhaka commits no further offence during a two-year probationary period. The 34-year-old said he had already paid the court costs. “A few weeks ago, I spoke personally here and said that I would take responsibility for my decision. I stand by that,” Xhaka wrote in German on Instagram. “I was sentenced by summary judgment for obtaining a false certification to a suspended fine of 50 daily rates of CHF 3,000 each, with a probationary period of two years. This means: The sentence will not be enforced if I do not commit any further offences during this time. I have already paid the court costs.

Oct 8 : Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho joked that he may not live to see the end of Manchester City's legal battle with the Premier League after the club appealed a ruling that found it guilty of serious financial rule breaches. An independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, as well as three of four charges relating to failures to cooperate with the investigation. City have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal. The Premier League said that City used "sham" commercial agreements to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.19 billion) over nearly a decade, resulting in inaccurate financial reporting and breaches of spending rules. Mourinho managed Manchester United from 2016-18 and led them to a second-placed Premier League finish behind Pep Guardiola's City in 2017-18.

FAST

LAUSANNE, Switzerland, Oct 8 : A speedy resolution to Senegal's appeal after being stripped of the Africa Cup of Nations title has been promised by the Court of Arbitration for Sport, who heard arguments on Thursday and will have a decision in days. Senegal are contesting the Confederation of African Football's decision to declare Morocco champions, despite Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time in January's final in Rabat. Senegal walked off the pitch for 14 minutes after a penalty was awarded against them late in regulation time, with several players returning to the dressing room in protest before they resumed play.  Morocco failed to convert the spot kick, sending the match into extra time, where Senegal scored the winner to secure victory.

However, they were stripped of the title two months later after CAF's Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch, overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 victory to Morocco.  Senegal quickly followed with an appeal to sport's highest court CAS, which was lodged on March 25 but heard on Thursday. "I know it's a long wait for the fans a few months after the final between Senegal and Morocco,” said CAS Director General Matthieu Reeb. “The timetable and the procedural calendar were established with the agreement of the parties involved in this case. So everybody knew about the timeline, and our objective as CAS, as the last instance authority, is to provide a reasoned award as soon as possible after the hearing today,” he told reporters. The long-running saga over the winner of this year’s Africa Cup of Nations title will be concluded within days although Reeb did not give a definite date. “I expect the decision to come not today, not tomorrow, but a few days later. The facts are set, are clear and the discussions will be on some procedural issues and legal aspects," he added. The CAS panel, presided over by French sports law expert Gerald Simon with assistance from Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based attorney and professor of law at the University of Zurich Ulrich Haas, heard the pleadings of the parties who were represented by their lawyers, with the hearing completed on Thursday. Morocco's delegation did not speak to media. Senegal General Secretary Abdoulaye Sow said they were confident. “But the important thing is that sports law is upheld and that this particular match is put to bed, for the sake of dignity and for Africa,” Sow told reporters outside the hearing, which was held behind closed doors.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Durban; Editing by Ken Ferris)

item.title: インフレリスクは上振れ方向で一致、成長には下押し要因＝ＥＣＢ議事要旨
item.description:
Balazs Koranyi
[フランクフルト ８日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が８日に公表した９月９─１...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
インフレリスクは上振れ方向で一致、成長には下押し要因＝ＥＣＢ議事要旨 0:56 配信

2018年4月26日、欧州中央銀行（ECB）　REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach/File Photo

Balazs Koranyi

[フランクフルト ８日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が８日に公表した９月９─１０日のＥＣＢ理事会の議事要旨で、エネルギー価格の極めて大きな変動と広範な不確実性を踏まえ、インフレリスクは一段の上振れに傾いているとの認識で全員が一致した。

ＥＣＢは同理事会で、政策金利を０．２５％ポイント引き上げると決定した。

インフレ率は既に目標の２％のほぼ２倍に達し、エネルギー高の影響でさらに上昇する可能性があるため、市場はあと２─３回の利上げを見込んでいる。

理事会は、エネルギー高が他の財・サービス価格や賃金へ波及する「間接効果」や「第二次波及効果」を警戒した。ただし現時点では、賃金の大幅な加速や広範な物価上昇が明確に生じたとは言えないという評価も示された。

経済見通しについては、リスクは依然として下方に偏っているとはいえ、以前よりもバランスが取れているとした。

ただ、金融市場の急激な調整がなくても、世界的な人工知能（ＡＩ）ブームの勢いが鈍化するだけで、世界需要と純輸出を通じた波及効果によりユーロ圏の成長見通しに重しとなるのに十分だとの主張もあった。

さらに、長期金利のさらなる上昇は成長に悪影響を及ぼす可能性があるとの指摘もなされた。

財政見通しについては、最近の政府支出の増加と長期国債利回りの上昇は、時間の経過とともに脆弱性を高める可能性があると示唆。健全な公的財政を維持することが重要だとし、エネルギーショックへの財政対応は一時的かつ的を絞ったものであるべきと指摘された。

ユーロ圏の長期利回りは７月の理事会以降、上昇している。これについては、長期ゾーンにおける最近の動きは、主に実質ターム・プレミアムの上昇によって引き起こされたように見え、これは官民の債務発行の増加と財政見通しに関する不確実性によって説明できる可能性があるとした。

７月理事会以降の市場金利の上昇については、世界的な長期利回りの動向とその要因の双方を分析し、金融状況、公的財政、マクロ経済を含む利回りの緩やかな上昇の影響を理解し、さらなる動向を評価することが重要だとした。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＥＣＢ「予防的」追加利上げへ、米イラン紛争長期化で アングル：ＥＣＢ、金利据え置きへ　原油価格が再び焦点 アングル：ＡＩの経済金融への影響、ＥＣＢフォーラムで希望と懸念が交錯 アングル：金融市場はＥＣＢのタカ派化見込む、イラン戦による油価高騰で コラム：求むＥＣＢ総裁、危機に強い革新者 最終更新: 10/9(金) 0:56 ロイター

Oct 8 : Ireland women's manager Carla Ward said she remained "obsessed" with reaching next year's World Cup and would not allow media speculation linking her with a return to Aston Villa to distract her from the playoffs. Ward's Ireland team visit Kazakhstan on Friday in the first leg of their round one playoff, with the winners facing either Poland or Belgium in another two-legged tie for a place in the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil. Villa recently dismissed Natalia Arroyo and placed Brian Sorensen, the club's technical adviser, in interim charge. Sorensen had only recently been appointed as Ward's assistant with Ireland, but was subsequently unable to take up the role. Ward spent three seasons in charge at Villa before stepping away in May 2024 to take a break for family reasons and was appointed Ireland manager in January 2025.

"I think it's always nice when you see your name batted about with top jobs and it shows maybe the work that we are doing," Ward told RTE on Thursday. "But it doesn't faze me. My concern right now is four games. I'm obsessed with getting to a World Cup, obsessed with the next four games. Nothing can take my focus away from that because that is what I came here to do." Ward's Ireland contract expires at the end of the World Cup campaign, but she declined to be drawn on whether she would have preferred a new deal before the playoffs. "It's not of my concern, honestly," Ward replied. "My concern is four games, four games that we want to win, four games that I am literally obsessed with in terms of what we do, how we do it and trying to get there. "And you know what? When those four games are over, I'm sure we'll have... ask me then." Ward's situation contrasts with that of Ireland men's manager Heimir Hallgrimsson, who signed a new contract until the end of the Euro 2028 campaign, before his team lost to the Czech Republic in their World Cup playoff in March. "I can't comment on that," Ward said. "I can't comment on the timing. I can't comment on those decisions. All I can say is my focus is firmly on the next four games." Ireland are without suspended captain Katie McCabe for the first leg, but the Chelsea defender will be available for Tuesday's return game in Cork.

Source: Reuters

item.title: トランプ氏、エヌビディア株取引 160万ドル購入・一部売却＝資産開示
item.description:
Courtney Rozen
[ワシントン ８日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領が８月に半導体大手エヌビディアの株...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
トランプ氏、エヌビディア株取引　160万ドル購入・一部売却＝資産開示 0:54 配信

6月11日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

Courtney Rozen

[ワシントン ８日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領が８月に半導体大手エヌビディアの株式を最大１６０万ドル購入し、その後最大１００万ドル相当を売却していたことが分かった。８日に公表された資産開示報告書から明らかになった。

報告書によると、エヌビディア株の取引は、トランプ大統領が８月に行った数百件の取引の一つだった。

ホワイトハウスのイングル報道官はロイターに宛てた声明で、トランプ大統領のポートフォリオは第三者の金融機関によって独立して運用されていると説明。「全ての投資に関する決定は完全に独立した運用担当者によって行われている」とした上で、「利益相反は一切ない」と述べた。

トランプ政権は、エヌビディアの先端半導体の輸出規制緩和など、同社の事業に影響し得る政策を検討している。またトランプ大統領は同日、エヌビディアのジェンスン・フアン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）らに、科学分野における功績をたたえる全米科学賞を授与する見通しだ。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：トランプ米大統領、任期中の利下げは望み薄　市場は高金利長期化を想定 焦点：トランプ政権の影で歩み寄るカナダとＥＵ、準加盟提示でも見える限界 アングル：トランプ氏の「信任投票」化戦略、共和党内に懐疑論も アングル：米保守活動家カーク氏暗殺から1年、設立団体拡大も若年層にトランプ離れ アングル：米中間選挙が事実上の最終盤入り、トランプ氏の共和党に暗雲 最終更新: 10/9(金) 0:54 ロイター

item.title: ベネズエラ前大統領夫妻、米で追起訴 政敵や米国人への拷問共謀罪で
item.description:
Luc Cohen
[ニューヨーク ８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Luc Cohen

[ニューヨーク　８日　ロイター] - 米検察当局は８日、ベネズエラのマドゥロ前大統領と妻のシリア・フロレス氏について、同国での権力維持のために政敵や米国人を拷問したとされる容疑で追起訴した。

マンハッタン連邦地裁に提出された追起訴状によると、両氏はこれまでの麻薬密売罪に加え、拷問共謀罪の新たな容疑で起訴された。

検察側によると、ある事例では、マドゥロ氏は２０１３年に、クーデターを企てた疑いのあるベネズエラ軍将校の逮捕を命じたという。その後、ベネズエラ軍の防諜局員らは、同将校を尋問する際に、通電した電線で約２０回にわたり感電させたほか、手足を縛って数分間つるしたという。

また起訴状によると、２２年にはベネズエラ入国時に拘束された米国人が、マドゥロ氏の暗殺を企てたとして告発され、軍の防諜要員から殴打されたほか、腕や脚、性器に電気ショックを加えられるなどの拷問を受けた。

マドゥロ氏の弁護団は、コメント要請に直ちには応じなかった。

マドゥロ氏夫妻は１月、首都カラカスの自宅で米軍に拘束され、麻薬密輸の罪でニューヨークに移送された。公判は２７年６月１日に始まる予定で、両氏は無罪を主張している。

FAST

BERLIN, Oct 8 : UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin will seek another term as head of European soccer's governing body, removing one of the highest-profile figures from the field of potential candidates to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency in March. Ceferin told the presidents and general secretaries of UEFA's 55 national associations in Berlin on Thursday that he would stand for a final term, reversing his previous decision to step down when his current term ends. The Slovenian said in August he would not stand against Infantino in FIFA's presidential election and confirmed his intention on Thursday to stand for reelection at the 51st UEFA Ordinary Congress in Astana, Kazakhstan, on April 22. "I want to thank the national associations for their trust," Ceferin said. "We have faced extraordinary challenges over the past years, and we have faced them as one team. There is still important work ahead, and I have therefore accepted their request (to stand again)."

His announcement came as UEFA's national associations continued their push for change at FIFA. UEFA said on Thursday that all 55 national associations except Azerbaijan supported FIFA reform proposals. "The national associations reiterated that they have lost confidence in the current FIFA leadership," UEFA said. "Institutional reform will not, on its own, be enough.  "FIFA also needs new leadership: a respected and unifying figure, deeply rooted in football, with the vision and experience to lead, the ability to command confidence across regions and an unequivocal commitment to development, reform, integrity and independence." Former Switzerland defender Ramon Vega said on Wednesday he intends to stand in next year's FIFA election against compatriot Infantino, becoming the first person to publicly declare his intention to challenge the incumbent ahead of the November 18 deadline. Infantino has faced mounting opposition since his failed attempt in July to bring private investors into a new FIFA commercial entity holding rights linked to competitions including the World Cup. Infantino has proposed an independent review of the world soccer governing body's decision-making and would propose consultations with confederations, member associations and other stakeholders on strengthening FIFA's decision-making.

item.title: AI pricing lawsuit against McDonald's raises new antitrust questions
item.description: A federal antitrust lawsuit against McDonald's this week claims the fast-food giant is using AI-powered tools to fix menu prices, marking the latest case to allege companies are relying on new technologies to collude and harm consumers.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: A federal antitrust lawsuit against McDonald's (MCD.N) this week claims the fast-food giant is using AI-powered tools to fix menu prices, marking the latest case to allege companies are relying on new technologies to collude and harm consumers. Plaintiffs have sued companies in industries ranging from hotels and real estate to health insurance, and now, hamburgers. The claims are pending in class action lawsuits around the country, with mixed outcomes so far. The McDonald's case hinges in part on the company's franchise model, in which most of its 14,000 US restaurants are independently owned. It says restaurant owners should be competing freely but are pressured by McDonald's to use its "pricing engine" or risk losing their franchise status, driving up the cost of Big Macs, fries and other menu items for millions of customers. McDonald’s told Reuters that its franchisees set prices individually, and that "AI does not set the price of a Big Mac or any other menu item.” The lawsuit followed a [USN:L6N45K103 TEXT:"Reuters report"] detailing how McDonald's is using AI to guide menu prices. The proposed class action in Chicago federal court says the company leverages its technology “to nickel-and-dime consumers down to the last French fry." NEW TECHNOLOGY, OLD LAWS Courts are still grappling with how to apply decades-old antitrust laws to AI and other modern software tools that can help companies instantly share and adjust pricing decisions. There's nothing inherently illegal about using computer algorithms to make business decisions on matters like pricing, courts have said. However, antitrust law can bar businesses that compete against each other from using such tools to coordinate their decision-making when it raises consumer costs. New technologies are giving competing companies access and insight into each other's pricing decisions, opening them up to claims that they are coordinating illegally, said antitrust expert Maurice Stucke, who teaches at the University of Tennessee's law school. In many of the pending cases, companies allegedly pooled pricing data using a shared third-party vendor. “As more companies outsource pricing to an algorithm, you can expect them to have more instances of collusion,” Stucke said. The results have been mixed in the lawsuits filed so far. In an opinion in July, a federal appeals court sided with plaintiffs by [USN:L6N43V12X TEXT:"reinstating"] a lawsuit claiming Atlantic City casino-hotels used shared pricing software to push up room rates. The Philadelphia-based 3rd US Circuit Court of Appeals said technical limits on communication in the past made collusion more difficult. "Today, these algorithms have the capacity to bridge any such gaps,” the court said. Other courts have been less receptive to similar claims. The San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals last year [USN:L1N3U70PW TEXT:"rejected"] a lawsuit against major Las Vegas hotels, finding their use of shared price-recommendation software amid a rise in room costs wasn't enough to sustain an antitrust claim. One of the longest-running sets of cases, involving software company Realpage, has resulted in partial settlements but is still ongoing. Realpage, owned by private equity firm Thoma Bravo, has [USN:L6N3X00XP TEXT:"settled"] some lawsuits claiming apartment complex owners used its tools to artificially inflate rental prices, including a case lodged by the US Justice Department. The company, which denies violating antitrust law, notched a victory in another case last month when it convinced a federal judge in New York to block a new state law barring landlords from using algorithmic pricing tools. The judge [USN:L6N45M0ZG TEXT:"ruled"] that the state cannot prohibit "normal commercial conduct just because it is facilitated by software." PRICING MCDONALD'S MENUS The lawsuit against McDonald's appears to be the first to argue that franchises operating under the same brand are misusing shared pricing technology to overcharge customers. Most other cases have claimed anticompetitive price collusion among companies that operate under completely separate brands. Daniel Francis, who teaches antitrust law at New York University’s law school, said the scope of franchisees' independence to set prices will be a key question in the case. The restaurants may be separately owned, he said, but their franchise status means they naturally coordinate on their menus and how their food is sold. "These branches are just not competing with each other in any plausible sense: they are competing against other chains," he said. "The presence of an algorithm changes none of that." The lawsuit says 95% of the company's US restaurants are independently owned, and McDonald's polices them to make sure they adhere to recommendations by its "pricing engine." It seeks unspecified monetary damages for a proposed class of millions of customers. McDonald’s said in a statement that its technology does "not automate, coordinate or fix pricing in any way,” but allows franchisees to “make the best decisions for their businesses and customers.” Jeffrey Shinder, an antitrust lawyer who is not involved in the McDonald's case, said cases over algorithmic pricing are testing the law's ability to keep pace with technological change, and could multiply amid a public backlash against AI. "I would expect to see more of them," he said. (This story has been refiled to fix the hyperlink in paragraph 5.)

WASHINGTON, Oct 8 : President Donald Trump bought as much as $1.6 million and sold as much as $1 million in Nvidia stock in August, according to his latest financial disclosure, which was released on Thursday as he prepared to award Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang the nation's highest honor for scientific achievement. The new disclosure of the president's investment in one of the world's most valuable companies comes as his administration weighs policies that could shape Nvidia's fortunes, including rules governing exports of its advanced chips.  White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement to Reuters that third-party financial institutions independently manage the president's portfolio and replicate "recognized indexes, such as the Schwab 1000."  Huang is set to receive the National Medal of Science from Trump on Thursday. The award honors Americans who have made "outstanding contributions to knowledge in the physical, biological, mathematical, engineering, or social and behavioral sciences, in service to the nation," according to the National Science Foundation's website.

"There are no conflicts of interest.” Trump is also set to give the same award to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Google co-founder Sergey Brin on Thursday.  Nvidia's spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Oct 8 : Alphabet's Google Cloud on Thursday introduced the Gemini agent, a single AI agent for work that can answer questions, handle tasks, create content and write code. The move comes as tech companies race to sell AI that can work autonomously. The announcement comes after OpenAI's September launch of always-on agents called dots that chase user goals across apps on their own. Earlier last month, Meta released Muse, a personal AI agent that can shop, book travel, send emails and make payments for users. Alphabet shares were up marginally in early trading.

item.title: 米8月卸売在庫、0.5％増と速報値から下方改定 需要堅調で販売増
item.description: [ワシントン ８日 ロイター] - 米商務省が８日発表した８月の卸売在庫は前月比０．５％増となった。堅調な需要が販売...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米8月卸売在庫、0.5％増と速報値から下方改定　需要堅調で販売増 0:02 配信

倉庫に保管されたコンテナ。米カリフォルニア州フォンタナで2022年7月撮影。REUTERS/Lisa Baertlein

[ワシントン　８日　ロイター] - 米商務省が８日発表した８月の卸売在庫は前月比０．５％増となった。堅調な需要が販売を押し上げ、前月発表された速報値（０．７％増）を下回る伸びとなった。

７月は１．４％増だった。

８月は前年同月比では６．４％増加した。

企業は、主に個人消費と人工知能（ＡＩ）向け投資による旺盛な内需を背景に５四半期連続で取り崩されてきた在庫を積み増している。その結果、輸入が急増しており、８月の資本財の輸入は過去最高を記録。第３・四半期の設備投資が引き続き堅調だった可能性を示唆した。

８月の耐久財在庫は前月比０．８％増加したものの、非耐久財在庫は横ばいとなり、石油在庫は３．９％減少した。

卸売売上高は１．８％増加。７月は１．０％増だった。

８月の販売ペースで在庫が全てはけるのに必要な期間は１．１８カ月と、７月の１．１９カ月から短縮した。前年同月は１．２８カ月だった。
