item.title: US Army report cites systematic failures in 2025 helicopter and jet collision that killed 67
item.description: The collision of an American Airlines regional jet and an Army Black Hawk helicopter near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport last year that killed 67 people was the result of several systemic failures, according to a US Army investigative report seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The collision of an American Airlines regional jet and an Army Black Hawk helicopter near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport last year that killed 67 people was the result of several systemic failures, according to a US Army investigative report seen by Reuters. The previously undisclosed report completed in May made a series of safety recommendations and said the key factor was two broken radio transmissions resulting in the helicopter crew not receiving critical details from air traffic control. The report also found a number of other issues including technical issues with the Black Hawk and a pattern of helicopter crews failing to fly semiannual minimum hours. It said many helicopters in the Army battalion — including the one in the January 2025 collision — did not have Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance systems. The report also said Army work with the Federal Aviation Administration on helicopter incidents in the Washington area before the collision was lacking and a working group "did not discuss airspace violations, near-miss reports, or pilot deviations." National Transportation Safety Board Chair Jennifer Homendy said in an October 1 letter to the Army that it had made significant progress in addressing its recommendations from the collision. It added, however, that it needed to do more work as "the Army's aviation safety system failed to consistently detect, interpret, and act on signals of latent hazards, resulting in degraded safety assurance, organizational learning, and safety culture." The NTSB report on the crash in January found a series of failures by the FAA were largely responsible for the deadliest US aviation disaster in more than two decades. The Army report noted that the helicopter was not providing key safety location data, known as ADS-B Out, due to improper maintenance. After the incident, the Army issued an urgent safety message to inspect all Army aircraft transponders to ensure ADS-B Out functionality, and all 3,600 Army helicopters were inspected by July 2025. The report also noted the Army had not addressed issues that led to the helicopter providing inaccurate altitude data and proposed a series of recommendations to address the issue. It also said the Army needs more advanced night vision equipment for pilots. The Army report also faulted FAA air traffic control for using "non-standard terminology for directing air traffic and providing incomplete traffic advisories." The FAA did not immediately comment. The Army said in a statement on Thursday that it has implemented stronger training and surveillance checks and completed new helicopter safety inspections, and testing on altitude awareness. It also said it was pursuing an FAA data-sharing agreement to help identify potential midair collision risks. The report also called for improved training for military pilots around Washington and Baltimore commercial airports and for reviews of Army helicopter operations near major cities in the United States, South Korea, Japan and Germany. Congress is still debating aviation safety legislation after lawmakers passed competing versions. The family of First Officer Sam Lilley, who was killed in the collision, said the Army report shows "the system failed everyone that night. The Army’s report acknowledges failures involving known altimeter issues, near-miss reporting, training, risk mitigation and safety culture."

item.title: 米スタバ、チポトレ買収を模索＝報道
item.description: [８日 ロイター] - 米コーヒーチェーン大手スターバックス（スタバ）が、メキシコ料理チェーンのチポトレ・メキシカン・グ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米スタバ、チポトレ買収を模索＝報道 0:00 配信

2025年11月、シアトルのスターバックス店舗で撮影。REUTERS/Matt Mills McKnight/File Photo

[８日 ロイター] - 米コーヒーチェーン大手スターバックス（スタバ）が、メキシコ料理チェーンのチポトレ・メキシカン・グリルの買収を模索していることが分かった。英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）が８日、関係者の話として報じた。実現すれば、米外食業界を代表する２ブランドの統合となり、スタバのブライアン・ニコル最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が、２０２４年にスタバに移るまで率いていたチポトレに再び関与することになる。

報道によると、スタバはここ数カ月、チポトレへの買収提案についてアドバイザーと協議を進めてきた。

スタバの広報担当者はロイターに対し、ニコル氏の下での経営立て直しに注力していると述べるにとどめ、報道へのコメントを控えた。

チポトレはロイターのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

報道を受け、チポトレ株は約６％上昇。一方、スタバ株は約３％下落した。

ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、チポトレの時価総額は約３９０億ドル、スタバは約１０７０億ドル。

アナリストらは、スタバがなお経営立て直しに多額の投資を続けていることから、買収には大きな費用負担が伴う可能性が高いと指摘した。

イートロのグローバル市場ストラテジスト、ラレ・アコナー氏は「買収には多額の借り入れや新株発行が必要になる可能性がある。財務面で説得力のある根拠がなければ、投資家は本業への集中をそぐ高くつく買収と受け止めるかもしれない」と述べた。

アネックス・ウェルス・マネジメントのチーフ経済ストラテジスト、ブライアン・ジェイコブセン氏も「スタバは改革の途上にあり、投資家が期待しているであろう利益率の改善もまだ示していないことを考えると、買収のタイミングにはやや違和感がある。第一印象では、改革を加速するというより、奇策に走って道を誤るように見える」と述べた。

一方、チポトレは消費者が裁量的な支出を控える中、客足の鈍化に直面している。食品価格や人件費の上昇も外食業界全体の利益率を圧迫している。同社の株価はニコル氏の退任以降、ほぼ半値となった。

ただ、一部のアナリストは、買収が実現すればチポトレの海外展開が加速する可能性があると指摘する。ノースコースト・リサーチのアナリスト、ジム・サンダーソン氏は「この買収の可能性について評価しているのは、ニコルＣＥＯがスタバの欧州でのライセンス提携を活用し、チポトレをより積極的に展開する機会を得られることだ」と述べた。

item.title: 米、マイクロソフトなどの永住権申請手続き凍結 9大学も調査へ
item.description:
Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff
[ワシントン ８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Dan Rosenzweig-Ziff

[ワシントン ８日 ロイター] - 米トランプ政権は８日、不正の疑いを理由に、マイクロソフトやアドビなどによる高度な技能を持つ外国人労働者の永住権申請手続きの一部を凍結した。また、交流訪問者ビザの利用を巡り、米国内の９大学に対する調査を開始した。外国人労働者や留学生向けビザ（査証）の取り締まりを一段と強化した格好だ。

バンス副大統領は「あなた方は素晴らしい米企業だが、優れた米国人労働者を雇用しなければならないというのが、マイクロソフトに対するわれわれのメッセージだ」と述べた。

ソンダーリング労働長官は、凍結措置がマイクロソフトとアドビのほか、コグニザント、インフォシス、タタ・コンサルタンシー・サービシズ（ＴＣＳ）、ウィプロ、ＨＣＬテクノロジーズ、キャップジェミニにも適用されると説明。永住権申請に必要な労働認定手続き（ＰＥＲＭ）について、「新規申請の受理も保留中の申請の処理も行われない」と述べた。

労働省のデータを集計するPermtrack.appによると、マイクロソフトは企業別のＰＥＲＭ申請件数で最多となっている。

移民取り締まり強化を看板政策に掲げるトランプ大統領は昨年９月、高度な技能を持つ外国人技術者向け就労ビザ「Ｈ─１Ｂ」の取得に際し、雇用主に年１０万ドルの手数料を課す大統領令に署名した。

今回の措置は、現在のＨ─１Ｂビザ保有者に直接的な影響を与えないもようだが、雇用主がこれらの労働者の永住権取得を支援する一般的な経路を遮断する可能性がある。

米市民権・移民局（ＵＳＣＩＳ）のデータによると、２０２６会計年度に承認されたＨ─１Ｂビザ保有者を最も多く雇用しているのはアマゾン・ドット・コムで、ＴＣＳ、インフォシス、アップル、マイクロソフトが続く。

バンス副大統領はまた、ハーバード大、イェール大、スタンフォード大、マサチューセッツ工科大（ＭＩＴ）、ブラウン大を含む９大学について、交流訪問者ビザを利用して外国人研究者や学生を受け入れ、米国人労働者の賃金引き下げを招いていると非難し、調査を実施すると発表した。

デスポジート労働省監察総監によると、対象大学にはすでに召喚状が送付されており、「外国からの影響力や不適切な金銭的関係、あるいはビザの悪用が、連邦政府の資金による研究を損なっていないかどうかを調査する」と述べた。

item.title: US freezes Microsoft, Adobe, Infosys green-card applications over alleged fraud
item.description: The Trump administration froze on Thursday some green-card filings by Microsoft , Adobe and major IT outsourcers and opened probes into nine top universities, widening a visa crackdown it says targets fraud and protects American jobs.
item.dc:creator: Akash Sriram, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration froze on Thursday some green-card filings by Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Adobe (ADBE.O) and major IT outsourcers and opened probes into nine top universities, widening a visa crackdown it says targets fraud and protects American jobs. The twin actions mark the broadest strike yet against skilled-worker immigration programs — potentially cutting off a common path to permanent residency for foreign tech workers — while putting some of the country's top research universities on notice. "There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft," Vice President JD Vance said. He said the company laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B temporary worker visas and nearly 3,000 green cards. The announcement about the permanent labor certification process — PERM — came hours before Trump was due to give Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. Under PERM, required for most employment-based green cards, employers must show that hiring a foreign worker will not harm US workers' wages or job opportunities. Microsoft is the largest filer of PERM applications, according to data from the US labor department. The company said in a statement that about 80% of the H-1B applications it filed in the last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of current employees, not to hire new workers. In July, the company said it would [USN:L4N4380XC TEXT:"cut 4,800 jobs"], or about 2.1% of its global workforce. Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said the suspension would also cover Cognizant (CTSH.O) , Infosys (INFY.NS) , Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) , Wipro (WIPR.NS) , HCL Technologies (HCLT.NS) and Capgemini (CAPP.PA) . "We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," Sonderling said. He said these companies had since 2009 sought almost three million foreign workers, and had received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications. Amazon.com was the largest employer of approved H-1B beneficiaries in fiscal 2026, followed by Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, Apple and Microsoft, according to US immigration data. Vance said the suspensions would last "as long as it needs to," adding that the administration wants the companies to change how they hire. He said some companies post ineffective job ads, then cite a lack of applicants to justify hiring lower-paid foreign workers. Microsoft said in its statement that it pays its H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work. “The immediate financial impact on major technology companies may be relatively limited at this moment, but the longer-term implications for innovation and competitiveness could be much more significant," said Ken Mahoney, CEO of Mahoney Asset Management. Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, HCL Technologies, Wipro and Capgemini did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Tata Consultancy Services declined to comment. Nasscom, India's IT industry body, said Indian tech companies in the US had significantly reduced their reliance on H-1B visas, and relatively few of their workers sought green cards through the PERM process. CRACKDOWN WIDENS The suspensions are the latest in a series of steps against skilled-worker programs. In September last year, the Labor Department launched an enforcement drive called "Project Firewall" as a White House proclamation imposed a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions for workers hired from abroad. During President Donald Trump's second term, companies have faced growing pressure to keep jobs and production in the United States rather than move them overseas. The action comes despite closer ties between the administration and tech leaders, who are lobbying for lighter AI regulation. UNIVERSITIES UNDER SCRUTINY Vance also said nine universities, including Harvard, Yale and Stanford, would be investigated for what the administration called the misuse of exchange-visitor visas to undercut American wages. The nine schools also include Brown and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Labor Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito said subpoenas had already been served. D'Esposito said investigators would examine whether foreign influence, improper financial relationships or visa abuse were compromising federally funded research. “It could have an enormous economic impact on the whole US economy,” said Sarah Spreitzer, a vice president at the American Council on Education, which represents college and university presidents. International students historically spent $40 billion a year while in the US, she said. The probe deepens the administration's long-running fight with Harvard over foreign students. Last year, the Department of Homeland Security subpoenaed the university over alleged misconduct by international students and its compliance with immigration law. Harvard called that subpoena "unfounded retribution" but said it would comply as far as the law requires.

FAST

MADRID, Oct 8 : Spain's minority leftist government plans tighter oversight of future data centres ahead of an early parliamentary election set for November 29, Digital Transformation Minister Oscar Lopez said on Thursday. Spain is trying to balance data-centre investment from companies such as Amazon Web Services and Microsoft, mainly focussed in the northeastern region of Aragon, against concerns over the industry's consumption of energy and water and has drafted tougher water and electricity rules. Lopez said a decree regulating the fast-growing sector would not require parliamentary approval. "The government's intention is to move forward with that decree," Lopez told a conference on artificial intelligence, adding that ministries were still reviewing submissions from a public consultation and working on a common position. Amazon's AWS and Microsoft have said their plans in Aragon remain unaltered but both urged Spain to protect long-term investment by promoting legal certainty and predictability.

Source: Reuters

FAST

MANILA, Oct 8 : Asian countries are racing to raise their oil stockpiling capacity, complete a regional power grid and speed up renewables in response to supply risks laid bare by the Iran war. Southeast Asia has been worst hit by the energy impact as 80 per cent of the oil transported through the Strait of Hormuz from the Gulf flowed to the region before the Iran war began. "The most advanced efforts are support for the development of oil stockpiling systems in each country and regional joint stockpiling on (a) voluntary basis," nine Southeast Asian nations said in a joint statement issued along with Japan and Australia.  Japan agreed on action plans with its Asian partners to boost crude oil reserves across the region following a meeting of the Japan-led Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC), a Japanese state minister on trade said on Thursday.

After a separate session with Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, Japan's State Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry Takagi Kei said they had expressed a willingness to cooperate to strengthen Asia's oil stockpiling capacity. Philippines, which imports nearly all of its oil and fuel, will create a national reserve by the end of 2027, its energy secretary, Sharon Garin said on Thursday, adding that it could subsequently be converted into a regional stockpile. The Southeast Asian archipelago is the chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) this year. Garin said countries will decide if they want to host a regional oil stockpile, and also the terms of sale that should be determined by the country itself.  "In the Philippines, what we want is if there's any country that wants to store the crude or their petroleum products here. In case of any emergency the country gets priority on this on the stocks," she said. The ASEAN member countries also pledged to increase the share of clean energy in power generation, targeting 30 per cent renewables in total primary energy supply and 45 per cent in installed power capacity. The region is among the biggest laggards in green energy. Renewables make up 14.1 per cent of primary energy, well short of a 2025 target of 25 per cent, while green power has made up 33.7 per cent of total capacity since 2020 against a 2025 target of 35 per cent, the ninth ASEAN energy outlook showed this week. The countries also reached an enhanced preliminary agreement on developing a long-delayed regional power grid, which Garin called a landmark accomplishment. The concept of a regional electricity network was first announced in December 1997.   "The first study was to connect with 2045, and that's too far because that's 20 years. So they're reviewing again to make it a faster implementation," Garin said.

(Writing and additional reporting by Sudarshan Varadhan and Karen Lema; Editing by Alexander Smith)

Source: Reuters

item.title: イラン情報機関、ドイツ国内の米軍基地を標的か イスラエルが警告＝独誌
item.description: [ベルリン ８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ベルリン　８日　ロイター] - ドイツの経済誌ビルトシャフツボッヘは８日、イランの情報機関がドイツ国内の米軍施設、特にラムシュタイン空軍基地とシュパングダーレム空軍基地を標的にしている可能性があると報じた。

同誌は複数の西側情報当局者の話として、イスラエルが３週間前に米国とドイツの関係当局に対し潜在的な脅威について警告したと報じた。イランとの戦闘に関連する米軍の作戦や兵站（ロジスティクス）を支援する基地が懸念の中心になっているという。

この件について、在独イラン大使館とイスラエル大使館からコメントは得られていない。独国防省はコメントを控えている。

米欧州軍（ＥＵＣＯＭ）報道官は「インテリジェンス（情報収集・分析）活動に関する事項について議論するのは適切ではない。特定の脅威情報や部隊防護措置についてコメントしない」とした上で、「米欧州軍は警戒を維持し、欧州地域全体の安全保障環境を継続的に検証している」と述べた。

関係筋はロイターに対し、ドイツ当局はここ数週間、イランの活動活発化を監視していると明らかにしている。

米国は今月初め、イランに関連する脅威を受け、 英南部フェアフォード空軍基地からＢ１戦略爆撃機１２機全てを撤収。米軍は同基地のＢ１爆撃機をイランに対する攻撃に投入していた。

item.title: Not just a case of déjà vu in France
item.description: Implications of the current nationwide demonstrations over school conditions
item.dc:creator: Mark John
item.content:encoded: Hello. One of the questions that France-watchers inevitably ask as we try to understand the implications of the current nationwide demonstrations over school conditions is: How are they different from the many other street protests that country has seen over the years? As far back as the late 1980s, French schoolchildren were joining often fierce protests over university reform; then in 1995, there were the big public sector strikes over welfare reforms; in the early 2000s, anger once more spilled over onto the streets over then-prime minister Alain Juppé’s attempted pension reform and welfare cuts; nearly two decades later came the “gilets jaunes” and their protests over fuel prices and the rising cost of living. Now, hundreds of thousands of students, parents and teachers are taking to the streets to air longstanding grievances over educational under-funding. Is this, as the French say, just a case of “the more things change, the more they stay the same”? Well, not quite. “In the past, pretty much every time there has been strife, money magically appeared to calm things down,” Paris bureau senior correspondent Leigh Thomas told me of how French governments of the day have so often secured social peace at a price to the state purse. “But there’s not a lot of room to do that now.” This is the problem. Within the politically fraught confines of the French budget debate now taking place, this advanced G7 economy apparently has no money to fix schools where classrooms are [USN:L6N45M0ED TEXT:"infested"] with cockroaches and rats, or where temperatures can swing from freezing to sweltering depending on the weather. This time, things have come to a head with the government hemmed in by investors worried about rising debt in a country which has not balanced its budget since 1974. The yield on French 10-year bonds briefly hit a 24-year high of over 5%, making the cost of its borrowing even higher. The 2027 budget [USN:L1N45N09R TEXT:"presented"] last week by Emmanuel Macron’s government has done little to assuage concerns and anyway is likely to get ripped to shreds in the parliamentary process of the weeks to come. For now, fears that this could balloon into a wider euro zone crisis are probably overdone. For one thing, [USN:L8N45S0RJ TEXT:"the hit"] to French bonds is still nowhere near as big as it was to, say, Italian and Greek debt during the European debt dramas of the 2010s. And while [USN:S8N449067 TEXT:"policymakers"] have made it clear there is no justification at present for the European Central Bank to step in and support French assets, investors broadly sense that the ECB would act if the contagion spread to others. Unless the government can find the extra resources to treat the root causes of the current anger while not further spooking markets, the unhappy stalemate is likely to continue. And this is where the other difference with previous bouts of social strife comes in: the risk it will play well for the political extremes. Whereas in the past, mainstream politicians have been able to just about muddle through, this episode could contribute to their demise. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen was already leading opinion polls ahead of April’s presidential election; the question is whether she will be joined by her far-left rival Jean-Luc Melenchon, a strong supporter of the protests, in the head-to-head second-round runoff. If she is, [USN:L1N44N0WZ TEXT:"surveys"] suggest she will be heading towards the Elysee Palace. THE HEADLINES [USN:L8N45G0SP TEXT:"US and Russia explore gas sale to Europe amid Ukraine war"] [USN:L1N45T0MX TEXT:"Trump administration plans to charge international students $70,000 for work authorization"] [USN:L8N45T1VE TEXT:"Spanish woman whose eviction ignited housing protests dies at 87"] [USN:L6N45T1CQ TEXT:"Amazon makes fresh job cuts, mainly in retail division"] THE CHART Pensions are taking up a larger and larger slice of France's government spending. France has among the longest life expectancies of any advanced economy, and among the lowest retirement ages: just 63. THE PODCAST "Where you can see AI — where we're actually measuring it — is at the task level... I think what we're going to be talking about in the labor market is how many tasks are created and destroyed, not how many jobs, because that's AI's impact in the world of work. It's not taking over our jobs, it's taking over our work in certain aspects, giving some of it to the machines and some of it to humans." ADP Chief Economist Nela Richardson. On this week's Reuters Econ World, ADP Chief Economist Nela Richardson joins Carmel to explain how AI is showing up in the labor market. Watch the show here . THE REAL WORLD Myanmar: The Trump administration has begun [USN:L6N45T16N TEXT:"direct talks"] with Myanmar’s military-installed government, the highest-level talks since a coup in 2021 Brussels: Tesla is mounting a pressure campaign to convince European lawmakers to approve self-driving on the continent Eritrea: The East African nation is one of the world's most isolated . Is the Iran war changing that? THE WEEK AHEAD Oct 12-18: IMF and World Bank annual meeting in Bangkok Oct 14: US CPI inflation Oct 15: US retail sales

item.title: Starbucks has explored Chipotle takeover, FT reports
item.description: Starbucks has explored a takeover of Chipotle Mexican Grill , the Financial Times reported on Thursday, in a move that would reunite Chief Executive Brian Niccol with the burrito chain he led before joining the coffee giant two years ago.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Starbucks (SBUX.O) has explored a takeover of Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG.N) , the Financial Times reported on Thursday, in a move that would reunite Chief Executive Brian Niccol with the burrito chain he led before joining the coffee giant two years ago. The potential deal comes as restaurant chains wrestle with uncertain demand from inflation-weary consumers and rising operating costs, prompting companies to look for new avenues of growth while facing pressure to improve profitability. Starbucks has worked with advisers in recent months on a takeover proposal for Chipotle, the FT reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Starbucks declined to comment on the report, other than to say it is focused on its turnaround under Niccol, a spokesperson told Reuters. Chipotle did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Shares of Chipotle, which has a market capitalization of nearly $39 billion, were up about 6% on Thursday, while those of Starbucks were down about 3%. Starbucks is worth about $107 billion, according to LSEG data. Analysts said any acquisition would likely be a costly undertaking for Starbucks, which is still investing heavily in its turnaround efforts. "A deal could require heavy borrowing or issuing shares," said Lale Akoner, global market strategist at eToro. "Without a compelling financial case, investors may view the deal as an expensive distraction." Starbucks is in the midst of a turnaround under Niccol, who has prioritized customer satisfaction through investments in staffing and store improvements aimed at reducing wait times and restoring the coffeehouse atmosphere that helped make the chain a global brand. [USN:L6N44V1E6 TEXT:"Since joining the company in September 2024, "]Starbucks has committed at least $500 million to labor investments as part of its reorganization, contributing to pressure on profitability. As of the fiscal third quarter, adjusted operating margin was 14.4%, down from 16.7% in the same quarter two years earlier, according to LSEG data. Starbucks has reported four consecutive quarters of comparable sales growth under Niccol, but [USN:L6N43V1FM TEXT:"in July"] he said that "We have more work to do." "The timing of this would be a little weird, given that Starbucks is in the middle of their transformation and hasn't yet shown the margin improvement investors are probably hoping for. Instead of jump-starting the transformation, at first blush, this seems more like jumping the shark instead," said Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management. Chipotle, meanwhile, has been contending with softer traffic as consumers pull back on discretionary spending, while higher food and labor costs have pressured margins across the restaurant industry. Its shares have nearly halved since Niccol left the company. A potential deal could accelerate Chipotle's international expansion, some analysts said. "What I like about this potential is the opportunity CEO Brian Niccol would have to leverage Starbucks' licensed partnerships in Europe to expand Chipotle more aggressively," said Jim Sanderson, an analyst at Northcoast Research. As of the end of last year, Chipotle had nearly 4,000 restaurants in the United States and about 100 international locations. Starbucks, meanwhile, has roughly 40,000 stores globally, including about 18,000 in North America. Niccol joined Starbucks in 2024 after spending six years at Chipotle, where he was credited with steering the company through the aftermath of its food-safety crises and building out its digital business, helping drive years of strong sales growth.

item.title: 米国務長官、ウクライナ戦争は危険な膠着状態 米は和平努力継続
item.description:
Jonathan Landay
[リスボン ８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Jonathan Landay

[リスボン ８日 ロイター] - ルビオ米国務長官は８日、ロシアとウクライナの戦争が危険な膠着状態に陥っており、米国は紛争終結に向けた取り組みを継続する考えを表明した。

ポルトガル訪問中のルビオ長官は記者団に対し、ウクライナでの戦争が「恒久的かつ持続可能で、公正な形で交渉を通じて解決されることを強く望んでいる。われわれは今後もその実現に向けて尽力していく」と述べた。

ロシアとウクライナによる相互のドローン攻撃は、幅広い経済分野に広がりつつあり、エネルギー施設や製油所、石油・穀物を輸送する船舶、電子商取引（ＥＣ）倉庫、データセンターなど、幅広い標的が攻撃対象となっている。

ルビオ長官は事態の悪化について、「このエスカレーションは北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）加盟国の近隣地域における破壊工作に発展する可能性がある」ほか、「二国間戦争国が、より広範で危険な地域紛争へと急速に拡大する可能性もある」と警告。その上で、「この戦争は交渉による解決で終結する必要がある。早ければ早いほど良い。米国はそのための支援を行う用意がある」と強調した。

トランプ米政権はここ数週間、紛争終結に向けた和平協議の再開を模索しており、ウクライナの交渉担当者が９日と１０日に協議のため訪米する見通し。

item.title: ユーロ圏の財政政策、今後数年は成長の重しに＝ＥＣＢレーン専務理事
item.description: [フランクフルト ８日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のチーフエコノミストであるフィリップ・レーン専務理事は...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ユーロ圏の財政政策、今後数年は成長の重しに＝ＥＣＢレーン専務理事 10/8 23:10 配信

写真は欧州中央銀行（ECB）本部の看板。2018年4月、フランクフルトで撮影。REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach

[フランクフルト　８日　ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のチーフエコノミストであるフィリップ・レーン専務理事は８日、ユーロ圏各国では今後数年間は財政政策が成長の重しになる可能性が高いとの見方を示した。

レーン氏はフランスの銀行大手ソシエテ・ジェネラル主催の会合で、今年のユーロ圏経済は予想以上に好調だったものの、財政政策による下支え効果は弱まっていると指摘。ＥＣＢは２０２７年と２８年に財政引き締めが行われると予想していると述べた。

インフレ見通しについては、来年は食品価格に上昇圧力がかかるとの見方を示す一方、インフレ率は目標の２％に回帰するとのＥＣＢの見解を信頼すべきだと述べた。

また、ユーロ圏経済は人工知能（ＡＩ）関連投資によって後押しされているものの、その効果は米国に比べはるかに小さいと指摘。ＡＩ投資について「欧州経済を押し上げてはいるが、米国や、ある程度は中国で見られるような、成長を圧倒的にけん引する最大の要因にはなっていない」との見方を示した。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：年初来安値で確認する円の「現在地」、円安は欧州通貨高の裏返し＝唐鎌大輔氏 アングル：欧州の中銀関係者、米国との協調維持に不安　市場介入に懸念 アングル：欧州の猛暑、経済損失は過去最大規模の恐れ　観光の変化で南欧に大打撃 アングル：欧州熱波、マクロ経済面からの市場注目ポイント アングル：欧州、熱波で気候変動への無防備さ露呈　「適応」対策が急務 最終更新: 10/8(木) 23:10 ロイター

item.title: AkzoNobel, Axalta set to win EU antitrust nod for $25 billion deal, sources say
item.description: Dulux paint maker AkzoNobel and US peer Axalta Coating Systems are set to win EU antitrust approval for their $25 billion merger with a pledge to sell AkzoNobel's vehicle refinish business to address competition concerns, people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Yun Chee Foo
item.content:encoded: Dulux paint maker AkzoNobel (AKZO.AS) and US peer Axalta Coating Systems (AXTA.N) are set to win EU antitrust approval for their $25 billion merger with a pledge to sell AkzoNobel's vehicle refinish business to address competition concerns, people familiar with the matter said. The companies [USN:L8N3WU04N TEXT:"announced the deal"] in November last year, underscoring a wave of consolidation among paint makers to save money in the face of rising costs and amid uncertainties created by US President Donald Trump's tariffs. The European Commission, which is the EU competition enforcer, AkzoNobel and Axalta declined to comment. The companies, which met with the EU watchdog on Wednesday to discuss the deal and possible remedies, will put in their offer next week. This will then extend the current Commission's October 22 deadline by 10 working days. The EU regulator is expected to clear the deal after its preliminary review, the people said. Earlier concerns about the overlaps in the powder coatings business have been resolved, leaving the vehicle refinish business as the only issue to be addressed, the people said. Axalta exclusively makes coatings, with a strong presence in the US market. Rivals to the companies include BASF's (BASFn.DE) coatings business, Nippon Paint (4612.T) , Sherwin-Williams (SHW.N) and Kansai Nerolac (KANE.NS) .

item.title: 米新規失業保険申請19.7万件、4週連続57年ぶり低水準付近
item.description: [ワシントン ８日 ロイター] - 米労働省が８日発表した１０月３日までの週の新規失業保険申請件数（季節調整済み）は前週...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米新規失業保険申請19.7万件、4週連続57年ぶり低水準付近 10/8 22:41 配信

米マサチューセッツ州メドフォードにあるレストランの求人看板。2023年1撮影。REUTERS/Brian Snyder

[ワシントン　８日　ロイター] - 米労働省が８日発表した１０月３日までの週の新規失業保険申請件数（季節調整済み）は前週比２０００件減の１９万７０００件となった。９月の雇用の伸びが大幅に鈍化したにもかかわらず、労働市場の安定が続いていることを示唆した。ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は２０万件だった。

申請件数は４週間連続で５７年ぶり低水準付近にとどまっており、エコノミストらが指摘する「低採用・低解雇」の労働市場の状況と一致している。ただ、企業は好調な利益成長と株式市場のパフォーマンスを背景に人員を確保する姿勢を見せる一方、新規採用には依然として慎重で、職を失った人が新たな仕事を見つけることが困難となっている。エコノミストらはこうした傾向について、関税措置を巡る不確実性に加え、ディーゼル（軽油）価格を過去最高水準に押し上げ、他のコモディティー（商品）価格を上昇させている米・イスラエルとイランの戦争による不確実性が原因だと指摘している。

ネイビー・フェデラル・クレジット・ユニオンのチーフエコノミスト、ヘザー・ロング氏は「依然として『低採用・低解雇』の雇用市場だ。仕事があってそれを維持したい人にとっては素晴らしいが、求職者にとっては厳しい状況だ」と述べた。

申請件数は９月第２週以降、２０万件を下回る水準で推移。季節調整前の申請件数が１０００件を超えて増加したのはカリフォルニア州とイリノイ州のみだった。

週ごとの変動をならした４週間移動平均は２５００件減の１９万８０００件と、２０２２年１０月序盤以来の低水準となった。

９月２６日までの週の継続受給件数（季節調整済み）は１７１万６０００件と、前週から１万７０００件増加した。９月の失業期間の中央値は１１．５週間と、約４年半ぶりの高水準付近となった。

一部のエコノミストは、継続受給件数が依然低水準で推移していることが労働市場の緩やかな弱体化を覆い隠していると指摘。最近大学を卒業した人を含む一部の失業者が、職歴が浅い、または全くないために受給資格がないことが背景にあると述べた。

パンテオン・マクロエコノミクスのチーフ米国エコノミスト、サミュエル・トゥームズ氏は「低調な採用の中で、労働市場への新規参入者や再参入者の失業が引き続き増加することで、今後数四半期にわたって失業率に緩やかな上昇圧力がかかるだろう」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：米政府、借り入れコスト抑制へ選択肢狭まる　歳出削減以外ならインフレ加速も アングル：米移民摘発、過去最高の逮捕件数も送還難航　法的手続きや移送能力に壁 コラム：米財務省の借入拡大、債務問題の大きさに比べれば単なるノイズ 焦点：テスラ、ロボタクシー「サイバーキャブ」で試す規制の限界 コラム：日銀利上げの「美しいシナリオ」に弱点はないか＝上野泰也氏 最終更新: 10/8(木) 23:40 ロイター

Oct 8 : Spotify said on Thursday it had signed a new multiyear licensing agreement with podcaster Joe Rogan for "The Joe Rogan Experience", extending a partnership that began in 2020. The renewal has similar terms to Rogan's previous deal, which carried an estimated earnout of $250 million, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Spotify did not disclose financial terms and did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The show debuted in 2009 and was exclusive to Spotify from 2020 until the 2024 renewal, when it also became available on Apple, Amazon and YouTube. Spotify said new episodes would keep coming out each week on its platform and elsewhere.

item.title: Dozens protest in Tokyo after Marine accused of murder in Okinawa
item.description: Dozens of protesters lined up in front of Japan's Foreign Ministry on Thursday after a US Marine was accused of killing a woman in the southernmost prefecture of Okinawa, many holding signs decrying crimes by US service members.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Dozens of protesters lined up in front of Japan's Foreign Ministry on Thursday after a US Marine was accused of [USN:L1N45T08D TEXT:"killing a woman in the southernmost prefecture of Okinawa"], many holding signs decrying crimes by US service members. The case is the latest in a string of incidents stretching back years that have fuelled unease over the large US troop presence on the island chain near Taiwan and China, with US officials warning it could undermine ties vital to security in East Asia. Public reaction to Anna Yagi's killing, however, has been muted compared with the mass demonstrations that followed the rape of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US servicemen in 1995. Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Yagi, 39, in a hotel in the Okinawan capital of Naha last weekend and taking her wallet and backpack. Ballard denied the allegations, police said. Leaders of Thursday's protest spoke over loudspeakers about abuses by US service members and called on the government to respond, with others in the crowd rattling noisemakers in assent. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has called the killing "extremely brutal and heinous", and Tokyo said it had strongly protested to the US and demanded measures to prevent a repeat of such incidents. Japan hosts the largest overseas contingent of US forces globally. Most of the 18,000 Japan-based Marines are stationed in Okinawa, which the US held from the end of World War Two until 1972. That presence has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of personnel. The US on Wednesday began a 48-hour pause of military operations and a ban on alcohol while troops undergo training on standards and discipline. Service members have also been given a month-long curfew for a "period of reflection".

item.title: Securitize launches blockchain-based stocks
item.description: Digital asset company Securitize is launching blockchain-based tokenized stock trading in major listed companies like Apple, Nvidia and Microsoft, with tokens backed by underlying shares, the company said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Lang
item.content:encoded: Digital asset company Securitize (SECZ.N) is launching blockchain-based tokenized stock trading in major listed companies like Apple, Nvidia and Microsoft, with tokens backed by underlying shares, the company said on Thursday. Securitize will initially launch its tokenized stocks on the solana blockchain. The company said it expects its tokenized stocks will also trade on NYSE's forthcoming round-the-clock trading venue, as well as a planned trading venue developed by crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange. Securitize Stocks preserve investor rights and economic benefits associated with owning a company's shares, Securitize said. The stock products will be available to eligible investors in the US, European Union and other permitted jurisdictions. Securitize Stocks will initially be available to trade during extended trading hours, with plans to offer 24/7 availability in the future. The crypto industry says tokenizing securities [USN:L4N3T81FC TEXT:"could revolutionize markets"] by allowing shares to be traded 24/7 and settled instantly, boosting liquidity and reducing transaction costs. Although [USN:L6N3UW0SJ TEXT:"many tokenized stock products overseas"] are marketed like stocks, they rarely offer the same rights, disclosures and protections as traditional equities.

item.title: Amazon launches first Android tablets, raising prices and incorporating Alexa
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 8 : Amazon on Thursday unveiled a slate of higher-end tablets that for the first time feature its Alexa+ voice assistant and run on Google's Android operating system, a bet that consumers will pay more for premium devices after years of focusing on the budget end of the market.Seattle-based

Amazon launches first Android tablets, raising prices and incorporating Alexa

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 8 : Amazon on Thursday unveiled a slate of higher-end tablets that for the first time feature its Alexa+ voice assistant and run on Google's Android operating system, a bet that consumers will pay more for premium devices after years of focusing on the budget end of the market. Seattle-based Amazon had been working on the tablets under the code name Kittyhawk, as Reuters reported exclusively last year, to transition away from its more limited homegrown Fire OS operating system software, after years of gripes from consumers and app developers. Fire OS is a “forked” version of Android, with modifications to make it work like a unique operating system. Known as Alexa Tablets, the line features several different versions with starting prices from $230 to $500; all are made with aluminum cases, a switch from Fire tablets’ plastic. The new tablets will cost as much as $550, a big bump from Amazon’s more recent top-of-the-line Fire HD 10 tablet which cost upwards of $180, though the company often discounted them.

The top Alexa tablet, with 128 gigabytes of memory, for $550 compares with an Apple iPad for $450 and Samsung's Galaxy tablet for $550. The product revamp marks a new strategy under devices chief Panos Panay to move upscale and away from the inexpensive gadgets Amazon sold at or near cost to hook customers into using Prime Video, Kindle, music apps and the main e-commerce website. That focus on affordability came with compromises, like lower screen quality and battery life, compared with rivals Apple and Samsung and others. Alexa+, an advanced AI-powered version of the Alexa voice assistant, will feature prominently on the devices to help perform actions or answer questions using generative AI. Accessing Alexa+ on the tablets will require a Prime membership or Alexa+ subscription, Amazon said. Amazon is pushing the pricier devices as worldwide tablet sales are falling, down 12 per cent in the second quarter from the year before to 33.6 million units, according to IDC data. The US market, which has been especially hurt by a shortage of memory chips, saw sales plunge 32 per cent in the second quarter year over year, IDC data showed. The Seattle company held just 1.9 per cent of the global tablet market in this year’s second quarter, down from 8 per cent a year earlier, according to IDC. Apple is the leader with 34 per cent, followed by Samsung at 17.5 per cent. The tablet prices do not include a one-time fee customers have to pay to turn off advertising displayed on the lockscreen, though the highest-priced Alexa Tablet will not have the ads. It will require a one-time $20 fee to eliminate the ads, up from $15 for Fire OS tablets, a spokesperson said. Such ads help users “discover new content that’s relevant to their interests” and the revenue helps underwrite other innovations, the spokesperson said. UPGRADE FROM FIRE OS With Android, Alexa Tablet customers won’t be limited to the apps offered in the Fire OS app store, disdained by developers who had to make a third version of apps offered in the Google Play and Apple stores. And the built-in Alexa+ voice AI assistant helps to differentiate the tablets from others. Amazon has spent billions overhauling Alexa to power it with generative AI and make it more capable for connected homes, shopping and accessing third-party services like Uber and Grubhub. The service, free with a Prime membership, is unprofitable. Prior Fire OS tablets will still work, said the spokesperson, but she did not say whether Amazon will continue to maintain the operating system or app store. Earlier this year Amazon cut off support for older Kindle models, citing software maintenance costs as a reason.

Source: Reuters

item.description: AMSTERDAM, Oct 8 : A successor to ASML's most advanced chipmaking machine could be ready in about 10 years, engineers for the company and its optics partner Carl Zeiss said in a peer-reviewed paper. The tool, dubbed "Hyper NA", would print smaller circuitry while re-using much of the companies' existing tech

AMSTERDAM, Oct 8 : A successor to ASML's most advanced chipmaking machine could be ready in about 10 years, engineers for the company and its optics partner Carl Zeiss said in a peer-reviewed paper. The tool, dubbed "Hyper NA", would print smaller circuitry while re-using much of the companies' existing technology, the paper said, though challenges remain. The machine, which ASML has begun developing but has not committed to producing, matters for the company's future prospects, as well as those of its partners and competitors.  ASML had no immediate comment.

The company is Europe's most valuable by market capitalization, thanks to its monopoly on lithography tools that use extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light to print the tiny circuitry of AI chips. SMALLER, FASTER CHIPS The paper in the October issue of the Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning, Materials and Metrology says Hyper NA could print features as small as 5 nanometers, more than a third smaller than ASML's current "High NA" EUV tool.  Though chipmakers are improving chips with 3-D designs, smaller features remain key for speed and power usage, and lithography is a limiting factor. Among chip manufacturers, Intel has begun using High NA in production, while last month Samsung and SK Hynix said they would follow in 2028 and TSMC in 2030. The paper said Zeiss can already make mirrors precise enough for Hyper NA, and the machine would be barely larger than High NA tools, already the size of a double-decker bus. Beyond Hyper NA, the authors said, tools would likely need to use a shorter wavelength of light, still a matter for academic research.  They said ASML's current light source "can be reused as is" for Hyper NA, while mentioning in a note that an alternative technique with free electron lasers would not change the lighting system's design. Those remarks are relevant for US startups including xLight, which is developing free-electron laser light sources that Elon Musk has hinted he might favor at his Terafab chip plant in Texas, and for Substrate, which is pursuing X-ray lithography.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Un avión resulta dañado en el aeropuerto de Riad por ataques hutíes, dicen fuentes
item.description: Los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, intensificaron su letal campaña de ataques contra Arabia Saudita, con el objetivo de bloquear el espacio aéreo y las instalaciones petroleras del reino mediante lanzamientos de misiles que han causado la muerte de tres personas esta semana y han dejado un avión gravemente dañado.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: Los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, intensificaron su letal campaña de ataques contra Arabia Saudita, con el objetivo de bloquear el espacio aéreo y las instalaciones petroleras del reino mediante lanzamientos de misiles que han causado la muerte de tres personas esta semana y han dejado un avión gravemente dañado. El grupo dijo que había atacado el aeropuerto de Riad y advirtió a los trabajadores de que se mantuvieran alejados de las centrales energéticas, que serían objeto de ataques. La metralla procedente de una interceptación o del impacto de otro proyectil había dejado gravemente dañado el avión comercial perteneciente a la aerolínea estatal saudita Saudia Airlines tras incendiarse mientras estaba estacionado en una terminal del aeropuerto el jueves, dijeron tres personas informadas sobre el asunto. Las fuentes dijeron que, según se cree, no había pasajeros a bordo del avión en ese momento, pero no pudieron descartar que haya habido heridos como consecuencia del incidente. En un vídeo verificado por Reuters se veía una espesa columna negra de humo y llamas elevándose desde el aeropuerto de Riad. La oficina de prensa del Gobierno de Arabia Saudita, su autoridad de aviación civil y Saudia Airlines no respondieron a las solicitudes de comentarios enviadas por correo electrónico. Lufthansa y Air India anunciaron que suspendían los vuelos a Riad tras los ataques de los hutíes. Por otra parte, las autoridades sauditas dijeron que los restos de un misil interceptado habían impactado en una guardería y un complejo médico de Riad. Los hutíes afirman que están atacando al reino por su apoyo a las fuerzas gubernamentales en la reavivada guerra civil de Yemen. Arabia Saudita ha dicho que respalda una ofensiva del Gobierno yemení reconocido por la ONU para recuperar territorio de manos de los hutíes. El conflicto, que ahora se ha convertido en una extensión de la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán, ha añadido un nuevo caos a una región ya en llamas y amenaza con arrastrar a otros Estados a una agotadora lucha en las montañas, mientras Siria se plantea ahora desplegar tropas para ayudar a Arabia Saudita.

item.title: Thousands of Spaniards march to mark death of octogenarian at heart of housing protests
item.description: Thousands of Spaniards marched through central Madrid on Thursday to mark the death of the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her home ignited protests across the country and led to a snap election next month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thousands of Spaniards marched through central Madrid on Thursday to mark the death of the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her home ignited protests across the country and led to a snap election next month. Maricarmen Abascal, who died on Wednesday, had been hospitalised for severe anxiety and exhaustion since her [USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:" eviction"] on September 23. No cause of death has been announced. Protests over home shortages and surging rents following her eviction prompted Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call a snap [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"general election"] for November 29 after parliament rejected his government's proposals to address a mounting housing crisis. As the sun set in Madrid, thousands followed a line of Tenants Union members, dressed in orange vests and walking arm-in-arm, as they carried a wreath of flowers from a protest camp in central Puerta del Sol square to Abascal's former home near Retiro Park. "They're not deaths; they're murders," the protesters chanted. Several people who received eviction orders have died by suicide in Spain in recent months. Political leaders on Thursday traded blame and invoked Abascal's case in attacks on opponents. Left-leaning parties criticised conservatives who [USN:L1N45O0BD TEXT:"rejected"] legislation in parliament aimed at curbing soaring rental prices. Right-wingers said the leftist central government had been unable to tackle the crisis after eight years in power. Alberto Nuñez Feijoo, leader of the conservative opposition People's Party (PP), accused Sanchez and the Socialists of trying to exploit the housing crisis for political gain before the election. "We will not allow this attempt to manipulate the emotions of the Spanish people; all of this has happened during their eight years in government. It won’t fly," Feijoo said. In the Madrid regional assembly, opposition leader Manuela Bergerot of the leftist Mas Madrid party said Maricarmen — as she has become known across Spain — had died because of "miserable people who put gain above a person's life." She said the last thing Madrid regional leader Isabel Diaz Ayuso had done while Maricarmen was alive was "laugh at her" — a reference to Ayuso's quip on September 28: "At what age do I get to stop paying my landlords? Let me know." Ayuso blamed Sanchez, saying Maricarmen had been evicted under his government. PROTESTERS BLAME 'GREEDY' LANDLORDS News of the octogenarian's death enraged protesters camped on squares in Spain's main cities who chanted that she had been "murdered" because of the greed of her landlords. After an investment fund purchased the building where she had lived for more than 70 years, Abascal lost a lengthy legal battle against rent increases far beyond her pension income, leading to her eviction. While in hospital, she reached a deal to regain her home but she died before she could return. "When everything is private, we will be deprived of everything," said a placard on Puerta del Sol square, where mourners lit candles and left flowers honouring Maricarmen. Outside Abascal's building, mourners left flowers, candles, handwritten notes and children's drawings. "Maricarmen was the straw that broke the camel's back... (she was) a symbol of resistance and unity," said Alex Marinero, a 21-year-old protester. Tributes to Abascal in the Madrid region's legislature also caused arguments as lawmakers accused each other of cynically exploiting the case. The PP, which has absolute majorities in the Madrid regional and local assemblies, refused to hold a minute of silence honouring her. Instead, hard-left deputies staged one outside City Hall and gave Abascal a 60-second standing ovation during a tense debate in the regional assembly, while PP lawmakers remained seated with folded arms. A survey carried out in June and published by state pollster CIS on Thursday found 76.3% of Spaniards supported intervention in the market to guarantee access to housing, while 79% believe the right to housing should take precedence over treating homes as a market commodity. Ombudsman Angel Gabilondo said addressing the housing crisis would require greater commitment from all levels of government. He said his office was preparing a housing report and reiterated proposals including expanding public housing, restricting tourist rentals, increasing rent assistance and strengthening protections against evictions for vulnerable households.

item.title: Man City head to Anfield under cloud of financial rules verdict
item.description: The Premier League resumes this weekend with one of its flagship fixtures, but Manchester City's trip to Liverpool will unfold amid a hostile atmosphere and beneath an unprecedented cloud following the club's guilty verdict in a landmark financial case.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: The Premier League resumes this weekend with one of its flagship fixtures, but Manchester City's trip to Liverpool will unfold amid a hostile atmosphere and beneath an unprecedented cloud following the club's guilty verdict in a landmark financial case. City head to Anfield on Sunday for their first league game since an independent commission found the club [USN:L6N45L10G TEXT:"guilty"] of more than 100 serious breaches of the league's financial rules over nine years, as well as charges relating to their failure to co-operate with the investigation. City have [USN:L6N45O0MF TEXT:"appealed"] the decision and continue to maintain their innocence, saying the commission's opinion contains "clear material errors" and that they possess evidence supporting their position. For now, however, the legal battle and the football season occupy the same uneasy space. City have carried on imperiously on the pitch, winning all five of their league matches to start the campaign, and will arrive at Anfield looking to preserve that perfect record. "The feeling is fantastic, to be honest," Maresca told City's in-house media on Thursday. "The players are excited for the next two games (they host Paris St Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday), but especially they are excited because in this moment, we are top of the league, so the players they are just focused on that. "They know that what we can control is the football side. They know they are professionals. They know that the noise is there, but they don't care too much about the noise. They are just focused on this moment, how we can beat Liverpool, how we can, together with the fans, try to win at Anfield." Liverpool, meanwhile, have endured a less convincing opening, with two wins and three draws from their opening five league games. That would normally provide more than enough intrigue for a fixture between two clubs that have shaped much of the top flight's recent history, but events away from the pitch have transformed Sunday's game into something far bigger. "If they want an understanding of how angry the game is going to be, then Anfield will tell them like you would never believe," former Manchester United captain and England defender Gary Neville declared recently on The Overlap podcast. "I suspect there may be banners, there will certainly be chanting. There will be a reception like you have never seen for them at Anfield... it will be a brutal day." SANCTIONS YET TO BE DETERMINED Every City appearance now comes with questions over what ultimately awaits the club, with the appeal process still to run and sanctions yet to be determined. The uncertainty has already prompted discussion over possible compensation claims from opposing teams and players and the broader consequences for English football. Anfield is hardly the gentlest place for City to return to domestic action after the international break. The rivalry between the clubs already carried plenty of edge after years of battles near the top of English football. Now Sunday's encounter will provide the first indication of how City's players handle the scrutiny generated by a verdict that reaches far beyond the usual rhythms of a title race. There is plenty at stake for sixth-placed Liverpool, too. Victory would provide an emphatic lift after their modest start and land the first blow on a City team who have so far been flawless. Defending champions Arsenal, who trail City by three points in second, kick off the weekend at home to Leeds United on Saturday. Mikel Arteta's side know victory would lift them provisionally level on points with Enzo Maresca's City. Leeds have provided one of the season's early surprises, sitting fifth after going unbeaten through five games. Another heavyweight fixture follows later on Saturday when Manchester United host Tottenham Hotspur, with both struggling sides desperate to inject some momentum into their seasons. United are 12th with just one victory, while Spurs are bottom with just two points. The meeting adds another layer of intrigue to a weekend already dominated by events at Anfield, with two traditional powers under pressure to turn around difficult starts when they meet at Old Trafford. Yet inevitably most eyes will be fixed on Anfield. After an unusually long pause in domestic football, the Premier League returns with its most contentious off-field controversy far from resolved.

item.title: Nvidia-backed Iambic Therapeutics launches IPO as biotechs buck market gloom
item.description: Nvidia-backed Iambic Therapeutics, which uses AI to develop drugs, is aiming to raise up to $159.4 million in its US IPO, as the biotech sector emerges as a bright spot in an otherwise lackluster market.
item.dc:creator: Manya Saini, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: Nvidia-backed Iambic Therapeutics, which uses AI to develop drugs, is aiming to raise up to $159.4 million in its US IPO, as the biotech sector emerges as a bright spot in an otherwise lackluster market. The initial public offering would value the drugmaker at up to $805.8 million — towards the top of its indicated price range — based on the number of outstanding shares listed in its prospectus, a regulatory filing showed on Tuesday. AI-driven drug discovery is among the few areas where the technology's promise is translating into growing investor interest, as biotech companies use it to identify drug candidates and speed up parts of the development process. Iambic is marketing roughly 9.38 million shares at $15 to $17 apiece. Investment firms ARK Investment Management and Duquesne Family Office have indicated interest in purchasing shares worth $60 million. Founded in 2019 as Entos, Iambic is advancing a pipeline of drug candidates developed using its AI platform to treat solid tumors. It has partnerships with some top pharma companies, including AbbVie (ABBV.N) and Takeda Pharmaceutical (4502.T) . "I would characterize it as a clinical-stage biotech company with an AI-enhanced drug discovery platform, rather than a pure AI play," said Kat Liu, vice president at IPOX. The valuation depends primarily on pipeline strength and the probability of eventual approval and commercialization, Liu added. A successful listing would set Iambic apart in a [USN:L4N45L0SK TEXT:"fall IPO market hit"] by a string of delays as rising Treasury yields and market volatility make investors more cautious. Concerns over an overheating AI trade and persistent geopolitical tensions have further dampened appetite, [USN:L4N45H0ML TEXT:"leaving biotech"] among the few areas still drawing interest. Iambic is aiming to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "IAM" after the offering. J.P.Morgan, Jefferies, BofA Securities and Citigroup are the lead underwriters.

item.title: Dólar baja cae a medida que los rendimientos de bonos europeos descienden desde máximos
item.description: El dólar bajó el jueves ya que se moderó la subida de los rendimientos de los bonos de la zona euro, mientras que las expectativas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal para este año se mantenían prácticamente intactas.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
item.content:encoded: El dólar bajó el jueves ya que se moderó la subida de los rendimientos de los bonos de la zona euro, mientras que las expectativas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal para este año se mantenían prácticamente intactas. Los rendimientos gubernamentales en la zona del euro volvieron a subir con fuerza, ya que el repunte de los precios del petróleo intensificó el temor a la inflación, y los inversionistas siguieron vendiendo bonos de países muy endeudados, como Francia e Italia. Sin embargo, el euro se recuperó de sus mínimos anteriores tras un retroceso de los rendimientos. El retorno francés a 10 años ganó 2 puntos básicos al 4,8873%, tras haber alcanzado un máximo del 4,9685% durante la jornada. Francia se ha visto especialmente afectada, ya que los inversionistas analizan minuciosamente su nivel de deuda, su déficit presupuestario y sus perspectivas políticas antes de las elecciones presidenciales de 2027. En España, los sindicatos anunciaron este miércoles una huelga general por cuestiones de vivienda para el 11 de noviembre, una protesta que tendrá lugar unas semanas antes de las elecciones anticipadas. Mientras, las expectativas de una subida de tasas de la Fed en su reunión de política monetaria a finales de este mes siguen siendo bajas, después de que las minutas publicadas el miércoles de la última reunión del banco central mostraron que los responsables consideraban la inflación como el mayor riesgo para sus perspectivas, y los analistas señalaron que no ofrecían sorpresas. El gobernador de la Fed Christopher Waller dijo el jueves que probablemente serán necesarias más subidas de las tasas de interés para reducir la inflación hasta el objetivo del 2%, pero añadió que existía "flexibilidad" en cuanto al ritmo de alzas y dejó la puerta abierta a una pausa en la próxima reunión en octubre. El índice dólar , que mide el valor del billete verde frente a una cesta de divisas, cayó un 0,08%, a 102,17, tras haber subido hasta 102,46, mientras que el euro avanzó un 0,08%, a 1,1204 dólares, tras haber descendido a 1,1171 dólares durante la jornada. La libra esterlina sumó un 0,07%, a 1,3219 dólares, después de que el gobernador del Banco de Inglaterra, Andrew Bailey, dijo que los Gobiernos deben redoblar sus esfuerzos para demostrar que pueden sanear sus finanzas públicas, ya que los mercados de bonos de todo el mundo están sintiendo la presión de los altos niveles de endeudamiento y las crecientes presiones inflacionistas. Frente al yen japonés , el dólar se debilitó un 0,12%, a 157,88.

item.title: Venture Global breached LNG supply deal with Galp, tribunal rules
item.description: Venture Global said on Thursday an arbitration tribunal found its Calcasieu Pass unit breached an LNG supply agreement with Portugal's Galp , marking the second setback for the firm over cargo deliveries from the project.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Venture Global (VG.N) said on Thursday an arbitration tribunal found its Calcasieu Pass unit breached an LNG supply agreement with Portugal's Galp (GALP.LS) , marking the second setback for the firm over cargo deliveries from the project. BP (BP.L) is the only other company to have prevailed in arbitration proceedings against Venture Global, as the US exporter dealt with a string of disputes with long-term LNG buyers, which also included Shell (SHEL.L) , Repsol (REP.MC) , Italy's Edison (EDNn.MI) and Poland's Orlen (PKN.WA) . Venture Global faces potential damages of billions of dollars from the disputes. The company has argued the spot sales were permitted, but two arbitration panels have now disagreed. Venture Global won its arbitration cases brought by [USN:L1N3U4117 TEXT:"Shell"] and [USN:L6N3YM1DM TEXT:"Repsol"], and subsequently defeated a court challenge related to the Shell arbitration award. It [USN:L4N40E1PP TEXT:"settled"] with Italy's Edison earlier this year, with Venture Global agreeing to supply additional LNG cargoes beyond those required under their long-term contract. Its only outstanding arbitration is with Poland's Orlen (PKN.WA) , which is expected to be resolved by the end of the year. The buyers accused Venture Global of selling cargoes on the spot market at higher prices following Russia's invasion of Ukraine instead of delivering contracted volumes from initial production at the Louisiana plant. Venture Global argued the spot sales were allowed as faulty power-island equipment delayed the start of commercial operations. Galp said in an emailed statement that it was reviewing the tribunal's decision and assessing next steps. The amount of money Venture Global will have to pay to Galp will be determined in a separate damages hearing expected in 2027 or 2028, with any final award not exceeding $170 million under the seller aggregate cap agreement, Venture Global said in its regulatory filing on Thursday. Capital One said in a note on Thursday that it views the $170 million liability cap as "relatively immaterial." Venture Global shares were up more than 2% at $13.34 at midday on Thursday. Venture Global added that one of the three arbitrators at the International Chamber of Commerce tribunal dissented and that it is evaluating its options while continuing to defend its position. The company also said the ruling does not affect the agreement currently being performed by the parties and noted it has delivered 20 cargoes to Galp since Calcasieu Pass reached commercial operations. After BP [USN:L3N3VQ1G3 TEXT:"won"] its arbitration case in 2025, Venture Global said in its annual report that the British firm is seeking at least $3.7 billion in damages, though the claim could exceed $6 billion before interest, costs and fees.

item.title: Euro zone ministers tell France to pass 2027 budget to calm markets
item.description: Euro zone finance ministers and the European Central Bank told France on Thursday to pass a 2027 budget to calm bond markets, as French borrowing costs hover at 25-year highs.
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski
item.content:encoded: Euro zone finance ministers and the European Central Bank told France on Thursday to pass a 2027 budget to calm bond markets, as French borrowing costs hover at 25-year highs. Euro zone finance ministers and the ECB meet in Luxembourg on Thursday afternoon for monthly talks and the surge in French borrowing costs was discussed. France is at the centre of a bond market storm on worries over the country’s large budget deficit and looming 2027 presidential election. Its 10-year bond yield has jumped nearly 80 basis points (bps) since the start of September and hit its highest level since July 2002, just short of 5%. That is driving up borrowing costs and making the fiscal maths harder. "It is essential that all member states, and in particular those with high deficits or debts, implement prudent fiscal policies," EU Economic Commissioner Dombrovskis, who took part in the ministerial talks, told a news conference afterwards. "Putting in place a sound budget for the next year will be important to ensure this predictability and credibility and to reassure markets. I'm in contact with,(French Finance) Minister Lescure on this," he said. France said in September that its budget deficit will overshoot the government's 5% target this year. The government has announced tightening measures to bring some calm, but investors are sceptical they can be carried out because of the fragmentation of the French parliament and presidential and parliamentary elections in April and May 2027. France also plans to sell a record €340 billion ($381 billion) of bonds in 2027 to fund the government and refinance COVID-era debt. "We have confidence in France's commitment vis-a-vis public finances," the chairman of euro zone finance ministers Kyriakos Pierrakakis told the news conference. Officials said no euro zone institution was ready to jump in to help France lower its borrowing costs. Officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, made clear it was up to French politicians to sort out the uncertainty they have created. The European Central Bank can buy bonds of a euro zone country on the secondary market, if their prices move in an unjustified way, to protect the transmission of monetary policy. ECB President Christine Lagarde told euro zone ministers the central bank had instruments to counter unwarranted, disorderly market dynamics that threaten the smooth transmission of monetary policy, but they were subject to clear eligibility criteria, according to officials familiar with the discussions. Published on the ECB website, the criteria include compliance with the EU's fiscal rules and not being in an EU excessive deficit procedure -- disciplinary action for countries with budget deficits higher than the EU ceiling of 3% of GDP. France is in such a disciplinary process with a budget gap above 5% of GDP. Its fiscal policies do not match the fiscal consolidation path agreed with the EU, so it would not be eligible for ECB help. Since the creation of the euro currency in 1999, France -- the European Union's second biggest economy and a key political player -- has only had a budget deficit below the EU's ceiling of 3% six times. Some officials said that debt markets were probably the only factor that could force it to consolidate.

item.title: ウクライナ東部要衝にロシアの爆撃、33人死亡18人負傷
item.description: [キーウ ８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[キーウ ８日 ロイター] - ウクライナ東部クラマトルスクで、ロシア軍による爆撃があり、少なくとも３３人が死亡、１８人が負傷した。当局が明らかにした。ロシアが掌握を狙う要衝で民間人を標的にした攻撃だと非難した。

今年最大規模の攻撃の一つとなった。警察によると、攻撃当時、現場の通りでは市バス２台が運行していた。ゼレンスキー大統領は、攻撃地点はバス停だったと述べた。

警察が公開した画像には、がれきが散乱する通りに複数の遺体が横たわり、バスとみられる車両の焼け焦げた残骸が写っていた。

フィラシキン州知事はメッセージアプリ「テレグラム」に「（ロシア側にとって）乗客を乗せたバスは格好の標的だ。１回の攻撃でできるだけ多くの人を殺せるからにほかならない」と投稿した。

地元当局者によると、ロシア軍はクラマトルスクをはじめ、ドネツク州の防衛の要となる「要塞地帯」の都市に対し、無人機（ドローン）や誘導爆弾による攻撃を強めている。

フィラシキン氏はクラマトルスクと、同じく要塞地帯の重要都市であるスロビャンスクの当局に公共交通機関の運行停止を命じたと明らかにした。

首都キーウのクリチコ市長によると、朝のドローン攻撃により３人が死亡、１４人が負傷した。

item.title: Moroccan defense firm MMI targets turret deliveries in March 2027
item.description: Defense firm Moroccan Military Industry (MMI) will begin delivering armoured vehicle turrets to the Moroccan army in March 2027, its general manager said, as Rabat pushes to build up its military industry with foreign partners.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Eljechtimi
item.content:encoded: Defense firm Moroccan Military Industry (MMI) will begin delivering armoured vehicle turrets to the Moroccan army in March 2027, its general manager said, as Rabat pushes to build up its military industry with foreign partners. MMI has a weapons systems facility in the Midparc industrial zone near Casablanca, while a second plant in Sidi Yahya, north of Rabat, is being established to manufacture medium and large-calibre ammunition, General Manager Kaduri Naor told Reuters on the sidelines of the Marrakech Air Show. Sources at the air show and earlier media reports have said MMI is closely linked to Israeli defense company Elbit Systems and uses its technology. MMI told Reuters it is a Moroccan defense company. Morocco and Israel resumed diplomatic ties in 2020 and signed a defense cooperation pact in 2021, opening the way for collaboration in air defense, artillery, drones and defense manufacturing. MMI has agreed with Morocco's defense administration to produce the turrets to be installed on 8x8 armoured vehicles assembled in Morocco by India's Tata, as well as related ammunition, Naor said. MMI is developing an anti-drone version of the same turret, targeting a rapidly growing global market as militaries seek lower-cost defenses against unmanned aerial threats, he said. "The threat is very cheap... defense systems are more expensive," he said, adding that MMI's solution was "cost-effective". The ammunition for the anti-drone turret will be produced in Morocco, equipped with a small radar that is designed to sense an incoming drone and trigger an explosion, dispersing tungsten fragments to destroy the target, he said. MMI is also planning to produce a self-propelled mortar system that can be mounted on vehicles, he said. The company hopes to use Morocco as a platform for exports, Naor said. "We will have a European NATO country to export to," he said, declining to identify the customer. Naor said 99% of MMI's staff, including engineers, were Moroccan.

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Simon Johnson　Johan Ahlander

[ストックホルム ８日 ロイター] - スウェーデン・アカデミーは８日、２０２６年のノーベル文学賞を、カナダの詩人で作家のアン・カーソン氏に授与すると発表した。「古典の伝統と戯れるように対話を交わしながら現代文学に新たな形式を創造した、大胆で独創的な作品」を授賞理由に挙げた。

賞金は１２００万スウェーデンクローナ（１２０万ドル）。

カナダの詩人・エッセイストであるカーソン氏は、トロント生まれで７６歳。２２年に国籍を取得したアイスランドで最近は過ごす時間が多い。 その作品は、詩、散文、対話、翻訳を融合させ、ジャンルの枠組みを超えた独自の作風で知られる。

古代ギリシャ文学の翻訳で広く知られ、こうした素養が自身の作品に色濃く反映されている。作品の幅はオペラの台本から文芸批評、１９９８年の韻文小説「赤の自伝（Autobiography of Red）」に至るまで多岐にわたる。

アカデミーは「話す時間はあまりなかったがカーソン氏は非常に驚いていた。今は風の音を聞いているアイスランドにいるとのことだった」と述べた。

アカデミーは「作品のほぼ全てで中心にあるのは、文献学者としての言葉への執着と、詩人としての新たな意味への希求が交わるところだ」と評価。「カーソン氏自身、自らの全ての作品の出発点として言葉の語源を挙げている。古代ギリシャ語からの翻訳は、それ自体が独立した作品と見なすこともできる」と指摘した。

Oct 8 : Italy's antitrust authority said on Thursday it had launched a probe into several Microsoft-owned video-game makers over their use of virtual currencies.  • Italy's probe is aimed at Activision Blizzard, among other companies of the Microsoft group, the antitrust authority said in a statement, without naming the others • Microsoft was not immediately available for comment • The move is part of a wider European Union-coordinated initiative by the EU's Consumer Protection Cooperation (CPC) Network. The network launched actions last month against nine video-game companies, including Riot Games, Ubisoft and Supercell, and had earlier opened a separate action against Microsoft-owned Activision Blizzard

• The aim of the coordinated action is to promote transparency and fairness in the gaming sector, particularly protecting the rights of minors • The probes focus on the transparency and fairness of in-game virtual currencies used to purchase cosmetic upgrades, weapon enhancements and other digital items, the Italian regulator said • Purchases are often priced in virtual currencies rather than euros and may involve multiple layers of conversion, making it harder for consumers to understand how much they are spending, the authority said • The Italian Competition Authority will act as lead authority, working together with peers in Norway and Denmark • The watchdogs will seek to determine whether the companies may have committed a "widespread infringement" of EU consumer protection rules affecting consumers in at least three EU member states • The coordinated action complements investigations the Italian regulator opened nationally in December into Microsoft group companies over the popular games "Diablo Immortal" and "Call of Duty Mobile".

item.description: ［東京 ８日 ロイター］ - ローソンは８日、アカウントサービスなどに不正アクセスがあり、個人情報の漏えいが判...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ローソンに不正アクセス、215万件の個人情報が漏えい 10/8 20:09 配信

２０１６年９月、東京で撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Toru Hanai）

［東京　８日　ロイター］ - ローソンは８日、アカウントサービスなどに不正アクセスがあり、個人情報の漏えいが判明したと発表した。対象人数は約２１５万件で、氏名や電話番号などが漏えいした。

１０月７日に実施した調査の中で、９月１２─１４日の間に不正アクセスを受けていたことが分かった。現時点で不正利用や二次被害の発生は確認されていないという。

item.title: 仏高校の抗議活動3週目に、政府が緊急対応表明 13日に再デモ計画
item.description:
Makini Brice Clotaire Achi
［マルセイユ／パリ ８日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Makini Brice　Clotaire Achi

［マルセイユ／パリ　８日　ロイター］ - フランスで８日、１０代の若者らが一部の高校を封鎖し、各地の都市でデモ行進した。抗議活動は３週目に入り、悪化する公共サービスへの対応を求める国民と、財政難に直面する政府との間の深い緊張を浮き彫りにしている。

パリのほか、北部リール、西部レンヌやナント、南部トゥーロンやマルセイユなど全国各地で大勢の人々がデモに参加した。

デモ行進は平和的だったが、パリとナントの一部では警察と抗議参加者の小競り合いが起きた。レンヌでは警察が群衆に対し放水砲を使用した。

ただ、教育省によると、封鎖されている学校の数は徐々に減少している。８日朝に２２４校だった封鎖校数は昼までに１５７校に減り、９６％の学校が開校しているという。

政府は教員不足や校舎の老朽化に対する不満に対応すると約束したが、具体策はほとんど示していない。

エドゥアール・ジェフレ国民教育相はランスで生徒や教員らと面会した後、欠勤する教員の代替要員を確保する緊急計画に着手すると表明。過密な授業日程も見直していると述べた。

フランスでは１０代の生徒が午前８時から午後６時まで授業を受け、さらに大量の宿題を課されることも珍しくない。

ルコルニュ首相は７日夜、１０月下旬までに「具体的で迅速、かつ財源を全額確保した対応策」を示すと約束したが、詳細には触れなかった。

生徒らの抗議活動を率いる代表者らは、これでは不十分だとして、１３日に再びデモ行進するよう呼びかけた。インターネット上では１０月１７日を抗議行動の日とする呼びかけも広がっている。

学生団体の代表は「昨日のルコルニュ氏の発言は空疎な言葉ばかりだった。抗議活動は続く。われわれは何一つ譲歩しない」と語った。

抗議活動が始まって以来、数百人が逮捕され、数十人が負傷した。１０代の若者１人が手を失う重傷を負ったことを受け、政府は７日、抗議活動の警備での閃光弾の使用を停止した。

＜大統領選控え、政治家の反応は二極化＞

大統領選まで半年に迫る中、抗議活動はマクロン大統領の後継を争う有力候補間の鮮明な対立を浮き彫りにしている。

最有力候補の極右マリーヌ・ルペン氏は、一部の抗議参加者が学校に与えた被害を強調。当選すれば公共支出を大幅に削減する方針を示している。

決選投票に進む可能性がある急進左派の対抗馬、ジャンリュック・メランション氏は、抗議参加者を「素晴らしい」と称賛し、警察の暴力的な対応を非難した。

調査会社エラブがＢＦＭテレビ向けに実施した世論調査によると、フランス国民の７２％が生徒らの要求は正当だと考える一方、５５％は抗議活動をやめるべきだと回答した。

８日にはベルギーのブリュッセル、シネ、リエージュでも生徒らの抗議活動が行われた。不満の対象は、費用の上昇、過密学級、教育資源の不足、教員の業務負担増などだった。

警察によると、リエージュでは今月、生徒らの抗議活動に関連して２００人近くが逮捕された。当局は１０月１６日まで、４人以上が公共の場に集まることを禁止している。

item.title: ペプシコ、北米不振で通期利益見通し下げ さらなるコスト削減へ
item.description: [８日 ロイター] - 米食品・飲料大手ペプシコは８日、北米におけるスナックや飲料の需要低迷および投入コストの上昇を...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ペプシコ、北米不振で通期利益見通し下げ　さらなるコスト削減へ 10/8 19:51 配信

ペプシコーラのボトル、ボスニア・ヘルツェゴビナのスーパーマーケットで2024年撮影 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/File Photo

[８日 ロイター] - 米食品・飲料大手ペプシコは８日、北米におけるスナックや飲料の需要低迷および投入コストの上昇を理由に、通期コア利益見通しを下方修正するとともに、さらなるコスト削減に取り組むと発表した。

ラモン・ラグアルタ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は発表文で「オーガニックベースで売上高成長を加速させ、投入コスト高の影響を緩和することを目的とした投資資金を確保するため、さらなる構造的なコスト削減策が検討されており、今後数カ月以内に実施される予定だ」と述べた。

同社の株価はプレマーケット取引で約１％上昇した。

同社は、為替変動調整後の２０２６年度１株当たりコア利益を１─２％増と予測。従来は４─６％増の下限を見込んでいた。

また、オーガニックベースの売上高は約３％増となる見通し。従来の予測は２─４％増だった。
